articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic periodontitis is a prevalent inflammatory disease that leads to destruction of periodontal tissues, resulting in tooth loss. While mechanical debridement and adjunctive antibiotics are commonly used, their therapeutic efficacy is limited by anatomical complexity and concerns over antibiotic resistance and side effects. Aloe-emodin (AE), a naturally occurring anthraquinone compound, exhibits significant anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial effects. However, its mechanisms in periodontitis remain unclear. METHODS: A network pharmacology approach was employed to identify potential targets of AE in periodontitis. The effects of AE on the viability, proliferation, migration, osteogenic differentiation, and inflammatory responses of mouse periodontal ligament stem cells (mPDLSCs) were assessed CCK8, qPCR and ELISA. In vivo, the alveolar bone of mouse periodontitis model was repaired and evaluated by micro-CT and histological analysis. RESULTS: Network pharmacology analysis identified 179 overlapping targets between AE and periodontitis, with key hubs including TNF, AKT1, EGFR, TP53, and MMP9. These targets were predominantly enriched in the MAPK, PI3K-AKT, NF-κB, and TNF signaling pathways. In vitro, AE significantly enhanced the proliferation, migration, and osteogenic differentiation of mPDLSCs while markedly suppressing LPS-induced expression. In vivo, AE dose-dependently reduced alveolar bone loss, improved trabecular microarchitecture, increased bone mineral density, and enhanced collagen organization in the periodontitis model. CONCLUSION: AE is a pleiotropic natural compound that reprograms the inflammatory-osteolytic microenvironment of periodontitis and promotes alveolar bone regeneration through multi-target pathway modulation.

articles.title: Systemic inflammatory response index: a potential mediator between substance use disorder and sleep disturbance.
articles.abstract: STUDY OBJECTIVES: Substance use disorder (SUD) and sleep disturbance share a complex, bidirectional relationship. However, the role of the systemic inflammation response index (SIRI) in this relationship remains to be explored, which will be beneficial for detecting SUD-related sleep disturbances. METHODS: Utilizing diverse samples from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) (n = 2,533) as well as self-collected clinical data (n = 88), we explored the associations among SUD, SIRI, and sleep disturbance. In NHANES dataset, weighted logistic regression and multiple machine learning (ML) models were employed to assess the relationship between SIRI and sleep disturbance, as well as SIRI importance in SUD group. Mediation analysis examined the role of SIRI in mediating the SUD-sleep disturbance association. During clinical confirmation, a two-sample t-test was used to discover differences in SIRI between opioid use disorder (OUD) and healthy controls (HC). Correlation of SIRI and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) was performed by partial correlation within OUD group. RESULTS: The analyses on NHANES datasets uncovered significant "SUD-SIRI-sleep disturbance" relationships, and SIRI ranked first in diagnosing sleep status of SUD subjects. Through validation via clinical datasets, OUD individuals also had higher SIRI levels and sleep disturbance risk than HC. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that SIRI statistically mediates the relationship between SUD and sleep disturbance in a cross-sectional context, positioning it as a potential adjunctive monitoring indicator for SUD-related psychiatric management. These results offer preliminary correlational evidence for mitigating sleep disruption through anti-inflammatory approaches, warranting further longitudinal and experimental validation.

articles.title: Complex antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and may reduce sudden cardiac death; however, the underlying antiarrhythmic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We investigated the cellular electrophysiological effects of the SGLT2 inhibitor empagliflozin in isolated cardiomyocytes from two non-ischemic, non-diabetic HFrEF models (rabbit and mouse). RESULTS: Ventricular cardiomyocytes from both HFrEF models exhibited prolonged action potential duration (APD), increased short-term APD variability (STV), and greater susceptibility to APD alternans and delayed afterdepolarizations (DADs). Intracellular Ca2+ buffering with EGTA prevented DADs, attenuated APD prolongation, and reduced repolarization instability. HFrEF cardiomyocytes also showed enhanced late Na+ current (INa,L) and reduced inward rectifier K+ current (IK1). Cell pretreatment with empagliflozin (1 μmol/L, 3 h), but not acute application (3 min), attenuated proarrhythmogenic AP changes, reduced INa,L, and increased IK1 in both species. Empagliflozin had no significant electrophysiological effects in healthy control cardiomyocytes. Selective inhibition of Na+/H+ exchanger-1 (NHE-1) with cariporide (1 μmol/L, 3 h) failed to reproduce the antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin under our experimental conditions; however, our studies were performed with intracellular pH buffered to 7.2, where NHE-1 activity is low. DISCUSSION: These results demonstrate that empagliflozin attenuates key proarrhythmic electrophysiological changes in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes. The requirement for drug pretreatment supports the hypothesis that empagliflozin acts through modulation of ion channel functional expression and/or post-translational regulation rather than direct acute channel effects in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.

articles.title: Sulfated polysaccharide-coated protein nanoparticles for enhanced delivery of psoralen in breast cancer therapy.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Psoralen (PSO) is an anticancer agent with a potential role in breast cancer management. Its clinical application, however, is significantly limited by poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. Therefore, the development of advanced PSO delivery systems is essential to enhance its therapeutic potential. METHODS: In this study, a novel nano-delivery platform was constructed by encapsulating PSO into zein nanoparticles (NPs) followed by surface modification with fucoidan (Fu), yielding PSO-Z/F NPs. RESULTS: Successful surface modification was confirmed by a reversal in ζ potential from positive values to -24.8 ± 0.02 mV, an increase in particle size to 129.23 ± 0.18 nm, characteristic changes in sulfate-related Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) bands, and the appearance of an S 2p signal in X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The PSO-Z/F NPs exhibited a uniform spherical morphology, with an encapsulation efficiency of 73.13 ± 0.98% and a drug-loading capacity of 5.40 ± 0.35%. Cellular uptake of PSO-Z/F NPs was 1.6-fold higher than that of uncoated PSO-Z NPs (P < 0.05). In vitro, PSO-Z/F NPs significantly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of 4T1 breast cancer cells. Specifically, wound closure rate decreased from 29.13 ± 3.33 % in the control group to 5.02 ± 2.86% (P < 0.001). Compared with the PSO group, the number of migrated cells decreased from 220 ± 33 to 146 ± 20 (P < 0.01), while that of invaded cells decreased from 144 ± 21 to 90 ± 8 (P < 0.05). Moreover, PSO-Z/F NPs increased the total apoptosis rate from 6.45% in the control group to 17.98% (P < 0.01). In addition, hemolysis assays showed reduced hemolytic activity, while serum-incubation studies confirmed improved colloidal stability, as evidenced by minimal changes in particle size and PDI over 7 days. Notably, in vivo and ex vivo fluorescence analysis of tumors and major organs in 4T1 tumor-bearing mice showed efficient tumor accumulation of PSO-Z/F NPs, and pharmacodynamic studies indicated enhanced tumor growth inhibition with an acceptable biosafety profile. DISCUSSION: Overall, PSO-Z/F NPs may provide a potential nanoparticle-based delivery strategy for improving the therapeutic application of psoralen in breast cancer.

articles.title: Hupehenine suppresses tumor cell phenotypes and modulates macrophage marker profiles in a diabeticmimetic colorectal cancer model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetes is associated with increased colorectal cancer (CRC) risk and mortality, but the molecular links remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize shared molecular features of diabetes and CRC, and identify compounds capable of modulating the candidate axis at this interface. METHODS: Shared disease-associated genes were identified using integrated bioinformatics and protein-protein interaction network analysis, followed by analyses of TCGA and single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Deep learning-based (DeepPurpose) and structure-based (AutoDock Vina) virtual screening were used to prioritize multi-target ligands. Binding was assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) and molecular dynamics simulations. Cellular effects were evaluated in a diabetic-mimetic model using high glucose, insulin, and palmitic acid (three factors; TF), with HCT116 cells and THP-1-derived macrophages. RESULTS: The IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis was prioritized as a candidate inflammatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface. TCGA and single-cell RNA-seq analyses associated axis-related expression with immune infiltration and macrophage polarization-related transcriptional signatures; higher axis expression was also associated with longer overall survival. Hupehenine (HU), a steroidal alkaloid, was identified as a multi-target ligand engaging IL1β, CXCL8, and CXCR2. SPR showed concentration-dependent binding (KD: CXCR2, 505 nM; CXCL8, 2.2 μM; IL1β, 12.7 μM) and interference with CXCL8-CXCR2 binding. In a diabetic-mimetic model, HU reduced HCT116 cell viability, migration, and invasion. TF-conditioned cells were more sensitive to HU than non-TF cells, whereas a corresponding increase in sensitivity was not observed for 5-fluorouracil or oxaliplatin. HU also decreased M2-associated and increased M1-associated macrophage markers. CONCLUSION: These findings support the IL1β-CXCL8-CXCR2 axis as a candidate immunomodulatory module at the diabetes-CRC interface and identify HU as an in vitro multi-target ligand. The observed changes in macrophage markers and differential sensitivity under diabetic-mimetic conditions warrant further mechanistic and preclinical evaluation, including direct assessment of macrophage function.

articles.title: The relationship of homocysteine and its redox forms with renal toxicity after high-dose methotrexate treatment in patients with leukemia or lymphoma.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: High-dose methotrexate (HD-MTX) chemotherapy inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, leading to impaired homocysteine metabolism, elevated levels, and associated clinical adverse reactions. Currently, studies often monitor total homocysteine (tHcy) levels, but its toxic mechanism remains unclear. OBJECTIVES: Given the association between HD-MTX toxicity and oxidative stress, this study aimed to analyze the correlations between tHcy and its redox forms with liver/kidney function indicators, and to evaluate their discriminatory ability for hepatic and renal toxicity. METHODS: A total of 310 blood samples were collected from 89 patients (38 adults, 51 children) with leukemia or lymphoma treated with HD-MTX. Concentrations of tHcy, free reduced homocysteine (Hcy), free oxidized homocysteine (HHcy, homocystine), and the ratio of Hcy concentration to HHcy concentration (Hcy/HHcy) were measured at 42, 72, and 96 h post-chemotherapy. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) were used to assess associations between tHcy-related redox forms and liver/kidney function indicators, and to compare concentration differences between toxicity and non-toxicity groups. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was applied to evaluate the discriminatory ability of relevant indicators for HD-MTX-related toxicity. RESULTS: In pediatric patients, Hcy/HHcy was significantly negatively correlated with creatinine (CR) (P < 0.028), and tHcy was significantly negatively correlated with alanine aminotransferase (ALT), total bilirubin (TB), and direct bilirubin (DB). No significant associations were observed in adult patients. Compared with the control group, the kidney injury group showed significant differences in Hcy and HHcy levels at 42 h (P < 0.05), Hcy at 72 h, and HHcy at 96 h. No significant differences were observed in the liver injury group. HHcy, tHcy, and Hcy/HHcy at 42 h all demonstrated good discriminatory ability for kidney injury, with HHcy showing an AUC of 0.817 (95% CI: 0.702-0.932, P < 0.01). tHcy at 72 h and 96 h showed reverse discriminatory ability for liver and kidney injury. CONCLUSION: Alterations in tHcy redox status after HD-MTX treatment, particularly changes in HHcy levels and the Hcy/HHcy, may be associated with renal function changes and may have potential value for identifying patients with HD-MTX-related nephrotoxicity.

articles.title: Persistent sarcopenia after flare remission in experimental RA responds to dipyridamole and is associated with restoration of adenosine and A2BR signaling.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with systemic inflammation and sarcopenia, which often persist despite successful control of joint swelling and the mechanisms sustaining it remain unclear. METHODS: Using the K/BxN serum-transfer model, we evaluated muscle structure, metabolism, and function after inflammatory remission. Dipyridamole was administered after remission of joint swelling to assess whether enhancement of adenosine and adenosine receptor signaling restore muscle homeostasis. Histological, molecular, metabolic, and functional analyses were performed. RESULTS: RA mice exhibited persistent loss of muscle mass, fiber atrophy, fibrosis, white adipose tissue expansion, and impaired strength and endurance despite normalization of joint swelling. RA muscle showed sustained myostatin (MSTN) elevation, Akt/mTOR suppression, impaired regeneration, senescence markers, and disrupted purinergic signaling characterized by reduced adenosine levels, diminished adenosine A2B receptor (A2BR) expression, and decreased AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activation. Dipyridamole administered after remission of joint swelling restored muscle adenosine availability, reactivated A2BR-AMPK signaling, suppressed MSTN, stimulated insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R)-dependent anabolic pathways, reduced fibrosis, and improved muscle function and fiber composition. CONCLUSION: RA induces persistent sarcopenia that remains after inflammation resolution. Post-remission dipyridamole reverses this phenotype in association with restoration of adenosine signaling, increased A2BR expression, AMPK activation, and enhanced anabolic pathways, highlighting purinergic modulation as a promising therapeutic strategy to improve muscle integrity and function in RA remission.

articles.title: Efficacy and durability of GB10, a novel bispecific VEGF/Ang-2 neutralizing fusion protein, in ocular neovascularization models.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the preclinical efficacy, durability, and ocular biodistribution profiling of GB10, a novel bispecific vascular endothelial growth factor/angiopoietin 2 neutralizing fusion protein, compared with faricimab in models of choroidal and retinal neovascularization. METHODS: Cynomolgus monkeys (cyno) with laser-induced choroidal neovascularization (CNV) received intravitreal GB10 (0.07, 0.7, or 7 mg/eye), faricimab (6 mg/eye), or vehicle. Dutch belted rabbits with DL-alpha-aminoadipic acid-induced retinal neovascularization (RNV) received GB10, faricimab, or vehicle. Chinchilla rabbits were used for biodistribution. Efficacy and durability were assessed by fluorescein fundus angiography in cyno CNV model and rabbit RNV model. Tissue concentrations were quantified by ELISA. RESULTS: In the CNV model, GB10 at 0.7 mg/eye achieved similar anti-leakage inhibition at a 9-fold lower dose relative to faricimab at 6 mg/eye (grade 4 incidence: 54.17% vs. 76.39% at week 1). By week 2, GB10 (0.7 and 7 mg/eye) achieved 0% incidence of grade 4 leakage, sustained through week 4. In the RNV model, GB10 sustained inhibitory activity for ≥12 weeks, whereas faricimab showed effects up to 4 weeks for FFA score and 8 weeks for grade 4 leakage. GB10 demonstrated high distribution in retina/choroid (≈35% of total exposure) and minimal systemic exposure (serum proportion 0.02%). CONCLUSION: In preclinical ocular neovascularization models, GB10 shows desirable efficacy at a 9-fold lower dose versus faricimab in cyno CNV model, alongside extended durability of ≥12 weeks (faricimab: 4 weeks for FFA score and 8 weeks for grade 4 leakage area) in rabbit RNV model. These preclinical findings demonstrate GB10's encouraging prospects as a next-generation therapeutic candidate, with efficacy profiles to be confirmed in clinical investigations.

articles.title: Cannabidiol alleviates anxiety-like behaviors via α3-containing glycine receptors in the lateral habenula.
articles.abstract: Cannabidiol (CBD) exerts potent anxiolytic effects, yet the brain nuclei and molecular targets mediating these effects remain poorly defined. Here, using behavioral and electrophysiological approaches, we identify glycine receptors (GlyRs) in the lateral habenula (LHb) as a key mediator of CBD's anxiolytic action. Pharmacological blockade of LHb GlyRs by intra-LHb strychnine induces robust anxiety-like behaviors, whereas both systemic and intra-LHb CBD administration alleviate them. However, CBD failed to reverse the anxiety-like behaviors induced by prior intra-LHb strychnine. Consistent with this, whole-cell recordings reveal strychnine-sensitive tonic currents in LHb neurons, implicating extrasynaptic GlyRs. To define the responsible subtype, we generated conditional knockouts and found that deletion of α3-containing GlyRs (GlyRα3 cKO), but not α1-containing GlyRs (GlyRα1 cKO), in the LHb produces robust anxiety-like behaviors. Notably, CBD exerts no anxiolytic effect in GlyRα3 cKO mice, establishing GlyRα3 as the subtype required for CBD's action. Furthermore, CBD elevates the action potential threshold and reduces the firing rate of LHb neurons, effects abolished in GlyRα3 cKO mice, thereby linking GlyRα3 activation to reduced LHb excitability. Collectively, these findings identify LHb GlyRα3 as a novel molecular target underlying CBD's anxiolytic effects and support CBD as a promising therapeutic for anxiety disorders.

articles.title: Mechanistic insight into circDDRC aggravated Cadmium-Induced DNA Damage: sponging miR-199a-5p to target PTEN and suppress PI3K-dependent homologous recombination repair.
articles.abstract: Cadmium (Cd), a pervasive environmental carcinogen, promotes pulmonary carcinogenesis through multifaceted mechanisms including oxidative stress induction and DNA repair impairment. Although circular RNAs (circRNAs) are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of genomic stability, their involvement in heavy metal-induced DNA damage remains poorly understood. Here, we identified a novel circular RNA, designated as circDDRC (DNA Damage Regulator by cadmium), and demonstrated its significant association with DNA damage through integrated analyses of occupational cohorts, in vivo animal models, and in vitro cellular assays. CircDDRC was significantly upregulated in Cd-exposed rat lung tissues and human bronchial epithelial cells (16HBE), where it exacerbated DNA damage. Mechanistically, circDDRC interacts with miR-199a-5p to regulate PTEN expression and modulate PI3K signaling. These molecular changes may disturb HR-associated DNA-damage-response cascades and aggravate Cd-induced DNA damage. Noteworthy, in Cd-exposed workers, the expression level of circDDRC was strongly positively correlated with both the Cd content in urine and the γ-H2AX (a biomarker for DNA damage) in blood, underscoring its potential as an early molecular biomarker for Cd genotoxicity. This finding highlights the critical interplay between environmental carcinogens and epigenetic regulators in disease pathogenesis.

articles.title: Enhancing transdermal permeation of berberine hydrochloride by Fu's cupping physical permeation-enhancement technique: a microdialysis study and mechanistic insights.
articles.abstract: Berberine hydrochloride (BHC) exhibits poor transdermal permeability owing to its strong hydrophilicity, and its delivery is mainly limited by the barrier function of the stratum corneum (SC) to hydrophilic substances. This study aimed to investigate the role of Fu's cupping physical permeation-enhancement technique (FCPT) in promoting the transdermal penetration of hydrophilic drugs and to elucidate its effects on SC structure and permeation pathways. With 3% azone as a control, the optimal FCPT treatment duration was determined using a Franz diffusion cell, and its in vivo penetration effect was evaluated by microdialysis. Confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) combined with fluorescent tracers was used to analyze the skin permeation pathways, and attenuated total reflection Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (ATR-FTIR) and Raman spectroscopy were employed to analyze the molecular structural changes of the SC. The results showed that FCPT treatment for 15 min produced the best permeation-enhancing effect, with the enhancement factor in in vivo microdialysis reaching 13.48 times that of the blank group and 167% higher than that of the 3% azone group. Furthermore, no persistent skin irritation was observed. CLSM revealed that FCPT exerted penetration-enhancing effects on both water-soluble and lipid-soluble tracers, suggesting that it may act simultaneously on the lipid and aqueous permeation pathways. ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy analyses indicated that FCPT disrupted lipid order and altered the molecular vibrational features of keratin, suggesting that keratin may undergo a conformational change. Collectively, FCPT acts on both the lipophilic and hydrophilic pathways within the "brick-and-mortar" structure of the SC, thereby promoting the transdermal penetration of hydrophilic drugs. This study also provides a methodological reference for elucidating the mechanisms of physical permeation-enhancement techniques.

articles.title: From laboratory to scalable manufacturing: Comparative analysis of thin film hydration, microfluidics, and impingement jets mixing.
articles.abstract: Lipid-based nanocarriers have established themselves as a cornerstone of modern drug delivery, offering a versatile platform for the encapsulation of diverse therapeutic payloads. Their utility spans from small hydrophobic and hydrophilic molecules to complex, high-molecular-weight biologics, such as proteins and nucleic acids. Although many manufacturing approaches are available, their effectiveness, scalability, and control over particle size distribution can vary widely according to the preparation strategy and process conditions. This study systematically compared bench scale thin-film hydration (TFH) followed by extrusion with scalable microfluidic mixing, and Impingement Jets Mixing (IJM), under standardized conditions. Liposomes composed of phosphatidylcholine S100 and cholesterol (3:1 mass ratio; final total lipid concentration of 10 mg/mL) were prepared using either Milli-Q water or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) as the aqueous phase, targeting particle sizes of approximately 100 and 200 nm. The resulting formulations were characterized in terms of size, polydispersity, ζ-potential, colloidal stability, particle concentration and phospholipid recovery. All manufacturing approaches generated liposomes within the targeted nanoscale ranges. For formulations targeting 100 nm, hydrodynamic diameters ranged approximately 90-125 nm in H2O and 75-130 nm in PBS, whereas formulations targeting 200 nm exhibited diameters of approximately 170-195 nm in H2O and 145-200 nm in PBS. Formulations targeting 100 nm generally exhibited greater colloidal stability and lower polydispersity, than their 200 nm counterparts, while particle concentration varied markedly among manufacturing methods. Despite these differences, phospholipid recovery remained relatively high (approximately 55% to 95% in H2O and from 55% to nearly 100% in PBS). Integrated NTA and phospholipid analyses revealed strong inverse correlations between particle concentration and estimated phospholipid content per particle in both H2O (Spearman r = -0.811, p = 0.0007) and PBS (r = -0.902, p < 0.0001). Overall, these findings demonstrate that liposome manufacturing technology should be considered a critical formulation and process-design parameter, as the selection of an appropriate production strategy requires the simultaneous consideration of product quality, material recovery, reproducibility, and scalability.

articles.title: Low-concentration photodynamic therapy induces oxidative stress-driven cytoskeletal remodeling and formulation-dependent cell responses.
articles.abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) induces localized oxidative stress through the light-activated generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), leading to targeted cell death. While conventional PDT protocols inducing marked photocytotoxicity have been extensively characterized, the cellular responses to low-concentration PDT, here defined as a reduced photosensitizer concentration under standard light fluence and irradiance, remain poorly understood. In this study, the effects of low-concentration PDT (0.33 µM) using pheophorbide a (Pheo), either in free form or encapsulated within poly(ethylene oxide)-block-poly(ε-caprolactone) (PEO-PCL) micelles, were examined in three cell models: primary human dermal fibroblasts, human HCT-116 carcinoma cells, and canine MDCK-1 epithelial cells. At the reduced Pheo concentration, PDT induced consistent morphological alterations across all models, including cytoskeletal remodeling, cell rounding, and early apoptotic features. These effects appeared earlier and were more pronounced with encapsulated Pheo, underscoring the influence of formulation on PDT efficiency. Antioxidant treatments (Sodium-L-ascorbate or N-Acetyl-L-cysteine) mitigated the morphological changes and cell death, supporting the involvement of oxidative stress in these responses. Compared with conventionally cytotoxic PDT, the low-concentration approach triggered slower cell-death dynamics, with caspase activation preceding plasma membrane permeabilization. Together, these findings show that low-concentration PDT induces oxidative stress responses across diverse cell types, while their magnitude and kinetics remain formulation-dependent. These findings provide a framework for further investigating the temporal and mechanistic dimensions of PDT-induced oxidative stress and their potential relevance to photodynamic priming, immune modulation, and combination therapies.

articles.title: Enhanced bioadhesion of thiomer-based hydrogels by tissue surface pre-conditioning.
articles.abstract: Hydrogel constructs often exhibit insufficient soft-tissue adhesion, limiting retention and therapeutic function. Here, a tissue-interface engineering strategy enhances hydrogel adhesion through sequential dithiothreitol (DTT)-mediated thiol exposure and UV-anchored multi-arm PEG-acrylate priming, enabling improved coupling with cysteine-functionalized alginate (Alg-Cys). Alg-Cys is synthesized by carbodiimide coupling and characterized by FTIR, 1H NMR, and Ellman's assay, showing ∼1200 µmol thiol groups per gram polymer. Cytocompatibility is confirmed using Caco2, C2C12, and HepG2 cells, and hemocompatibility is evaluated with human erythrocytes. Using ex vivo porcine tissues including small intestinal mucosa, skeletal muscle and liver, an optimized DTT treatment at 50 mM for 30 min increased accessible surface thiols in a tissue dependent manner, with mucosa showing the strongest response (∼2-fold). Subsequent PEG-acrylate priming further amplifies reactive surface functionalities, with 8-arm primers increasing immobilized acrylate groups up to 3.6-fold on mucosa, 3.4-fold on muscle, and 2.2-fold on liver. A 5% Alg-Cys formulation combined with 8-arm PEG-acrylate exhibits favorable rheological properties, shear-thinning behavior, and rapid structural recovery. Ex vivo adhesion testing demonstrates up to ∼2-fold enhancement in adhesion across all tissues. This sequential tissue activation strategy substantially strengthens hydrogel-tissue interfaces and provides a versatile approach to improving thiomer bioinks for in situ bioprinting and regenerative therapies.

articles.title: Niosomal encapsulation enhances thymoquinone-induced apoptosis in androgen-independent prostate cancer: an integrated DFT, docking, ADMET and cellular study.
articles.abstract: Thymoquinone (TQ), the principal bioactive constituent of Nigella sativa seed oil, engages multiple anticancer pathways but is limited clinically by a sub-hourly plasma half-life and rapid hepatic clearance. We report a Span 60/cholesterol niosomal carrier (TQ-NIO) evaluated in PC-3 and LNCaP prostate cancer cells within an integrated quantum-chemical and target-engagement framework. TQ-NIO formed sub-micron vesicles (341.2 ± 12.1 nm; PDI 0.63 ± 0.13; ζ = -29.1 ± 0.8 mV) with 81.3 ± 0.8 % encapsulation efficiency and Korsmeyer-Peppas-controlled Fickian release (n = 0.28) over 72 h. Encapsulation halved the WST-1 IC50 of TQ in androgen-independent PC-3 cells (24 h: 13.5 → 6.5 µg mL-1; 48 h: 9.4 → 4.1 µg mL-1), while shifts in LNCaP cells were minimal, a cell-line-selective response. In PC-3, TQ-NIO amplified caspase-3/-9 activation 2.6-2.7-fold, raised p53 (3.7-fold) and Bax (2.4-fold), and suppressed Bcl-2 (0.50-fold) and survivin (0.40-fold); HUVECs retained near-control morphology. Free TQ inhibited violacein production in Chromobacterium violaceum (zone 20.3 ± 0.6 mm), and the niosomal form preserved anti-biofilm activity against Escherichia coli at dilutions where free TQ failed. Calculations at the B3LYP-D4/def2-TZVP level assigned TQ super-electrophilic character (ω ≈ 7.3 eV) with C7/C8 as Michael-acceptor centers and O4 as the dominant nucleophilic anchor, while docking against five oncologically relevant targets returned modest binding energies (-4.70 to -5.78 kcal mol-1) indicating possible interactions rather than demonstrated target engagement or functional inhibition. Niosomal encapsulation enhanced the in vitro antiproliferative and apoptosis-associated effects of TQ, particularly in PC-3 cells.

articles.title: Folding Free Energy and Evolution Guided Rational Engineering of Arginine Deiminase Enables Enhanced Catalytic Efficiency, Structural Robustness, and Antitumor Efficacy.
articles.abstract: Arginine deiminase (ADI) is a promising therapeutic enzyme for targeting arginine-auxotrophic cancers, but its clinical application is limited by insufficient catalytic efficiency and poor stability. In this study, we developed a rational protein engineering strategy integrating folding free energy (ΔΔG) prediction and evolutionary conservation analysis to optimize ADI from Pseudomonas mendocina. A comprehensive site-saturation mutational scan was performed using the Pythia framework, followed by ConSurf-based filtering to exclude highly conserved residues, thereby efficiently identifying candidate beneficial mutations. Experimental evaluation showed that several single mutations enhanced enzymatic activity, and combinatorial optimization further revealed synergistic effects. Notably, the triple mutant K91L/N95E/Y346E exhibited the most significant improvement, achieving a 2.7-fold increase in catalytic efficiency (kcat/KM) compared to the wild type. In addition, this variant demonstrated enhanced thermal stability and improved plasma stability, with an extended half-life and higher residual activity. Importantly, in vitro cytotoxicity assays confirmed that the engineered mutant displayed superior antitumor activity against colorectal cancer cells. Overall, this study highlights the effectiveness of integrating thermodynamic and evolutionary constraints for enzyme engineering and provides a promising strategy for developing ADI-based anticancer therapeutics.

articles.title: A mechanistic pharmacokinetic-patient-derived organoid (PK-PDO) framework for comparing oxaliplatin HIPEC regimens in peritoneal metastases of colorectal cancer.
articles.abstract: The role of oxaliplatin-based hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) in colorectal peritoneal metastases remains debated after the PRODIGE 7 trial showed no overall survival benefit for the widely used 30-min high-dose regimen. This has raised interest in whether alternative oxaliplatin schedules, particularly lower-dose and longer-duration regimens, may improve tumor exposure and pharmacodynamic (PD) activity. In this study, we present a mechanistic framework integrating pharmacokinetics with patient-derived organoid (PK-PDO) data to compare two established HIPEC regimens for colorectal peritoneal metastases: 460 mg/m2 over 30 min and 200 mg/m2 over 120 min. A population-based PK model was coupled with a spatiotemporal transport model to simulate oxaliplatin distribution within tumor nodules up to 2 mm. Exposure metrics were integrated with published PDO sensitivity data, including IC50 and Hill coefficients, to evaluate response under dynamic concentration profiles. The long-duration regimen increased tumor-to-plasma ultrafiltrate exposure. However, overall PD efficacy at the population level, quantified using a Hill-type exposure-response model, was not significantly different between regimens. Substantial interpatient variability was predicted, with some tumors favoring one regimen over the other depending on drug sensitivity. Threshold analysis indicated that the 120-min regimen is advantageous only when its IC50 is at least fivefold lower than that of the 30-min regimen. In conclusion, despite differences in PK profiles, both regimens yield comparable overall PD effects. These findings suggest that switching oxaliplatin HIPEC protocols may not consistently improve treatment efficacy and that outcomes depend on the sensitivity of tumor nodules to treatment duration, as reflected by PDOs.

articles.title: Cisplatin induces skeletal muscle dysfunction, oxidative stress, and senescence-associated responses in male and female rats.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Cisplatin-induced skeletal muscle dysfunction contributes to functional decline, but molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated cisplatin-induced changes in contractile function, oxidative stress, senescence-associated signaling, and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) in soleus (SOL) and extensor digitorum longus (EDL) muscles of male and female rats. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male and female rats received cisplatin (5 mg/kg, i.p.) or saline on days 1, 8, and 15 and were euthanized 24 h after the final injection. SOL and EDL muscles were analyzed for contractile function, oxidative damage, antioxidant gene expression, senescence markers, SASP-related factors, and fiber cross-sectional area (CSA). KEY FINDINGS: Cisplatin caused body weight loss without detectable changes in muscle mass or fiber CSA. Contractile force decreased in SOL of both sexes and male EDL, whereas no significant reduction was observed in female EDL. H₂O₂ and protein carbonyl levels increased in SOL, whereas MDA and 8-OHdG increased in both muscles and sexes. CAT and GPX mRNA decreased in SOL of both sexes, while SOD, CAT, and GPX decreased in male EDL, with no significant changes detected in female EDL. p53 protein increased in both muscles of both sexes, whereas p21 and p16 proteins increased only in female SOL. At the transcript level, p53, p21, and p16 were upregulated in male SOL and female EDL. SASP-related genes showed group-specific increases in inflammatory cytokines and matrix-remodeling genes. SIGNIFICANCE: Cisplatin impaired contractile function without detectable changes in muscle mass or fiber CSA, with different molecular response patterns observed across the examined sex and muscle groups.

articles.title: Reelin-enhanced neural stem cell therapy promotes neuroangiogenesis, remyelination, and functional recovery after subcortical capsular ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: AIMS: This study established a reproducible mouse model of posterior limb of the internal capsule (PLIC) ischemia to investigate whether Reelin potentiates neural stem cell (NSC)-mediated functional and structural recovery, addressing the limited regenerative strategies for subcortical stroke. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A deep photothrombotic PLIC stroke model was induced in mice using a fiber-optic laser system. Embryonic NSCs were isolated from E14 embryos and characterized by flow cytometry, showing >85% Nestin positivity. Reelin effects on NSC viability were evaluated by MTT assay. Seven days after stroke, mice received intracortical PBS, NSCs, Reelin, or NSCs plus Reelin. Recovery was assessed by modified Neurological Severity Score. Histological, immunofluorescence, immunohistochemical, ELISA, flow cytometric, and ultrastructural analyses examined inflammation, endogenous and grafted NSC responses, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal repair, myelin preservation, and diaschisis. KEY FINDINGS: The optimized model produced consistent focal PLIC infarcts with marked motor deficits. Reelin increased NSC viability in vitro in a dose-dependent manner up to 200 nM. In vivo, combined NSC + Reelin treatment reduced TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6, while increasing IL-10 and TGF-β. It also promoted M2 microglial polarization, enhanced proliferation and neuronal differentiation of endogenous and transplanted NSCs, increased GAP-43-positive axonal regeneration and vWF-positive angiogenesis, preserved myelin integrity, and attenuated retrograde degeneration/diaschisis. These effects were accompanied by increased internal capsule volume and improved neurological function, together with histological and ultrastructural evidence of enhanced axonal integrity and myelin preservation. SIGNIFICANCE: The combined strategy promotes recovery by coordinating neuroinflammatory resolution, extracellular matrix remodeling, neurogenesis, angiogenesis, axonal regeneration, and remyelination. These findings support Reelin-assisted NSC therapy as a promising combinatorial regenerative approach for subcortical ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Polygenic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity patterns and major adverse cardiovascular events: Insights from a target trial emulation study.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Physical activity is a key modifiable lifestyle factor for cardiovascular prevention. However, precise prevention strategies regarding long-term physical activity are lacking, particularly concerning whether genetic susceptibility modifies the association between long-term physical activity and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Most previous cohort studies rely on a single assessment of physical activity, which may not capture long-term behavior. To address these gaps, we used repeated assessments and a target trial emulation framework in UK Biobank. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We studied 27,459 UK Biobank participants with repeat physical activity assessments. A target trial emulation framework defined eligibility, time zero, exposure groups, and follow-up. The prespecified primary contrast compared increased physical activity with sustained low activity after 1:1 propensity score matching. Secondary full-cohort models examined four physical activity change patterns. Cardiovascular polygenic risk strata were evaluated exploratorily. KEY FINDINGS: In 4401 matched pairs, increased physical activity was not significantly associated with lower major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) compared with sustained low activity (HR 1.19, 95% CI 0.90-1.58). In full-cohort models, sustained high physical activity was associated with higher MACE risk (HR 1.27, 95% CI 1.03-1.56). This signal was more apparent among participants with intermediate or high cardiovascular polygenic risk. SIGNIFICANCE: In this UK Biobank target trial emulation, increasing physical activity from low levels did not clearly reduce MACE, whereas sustained high activity showed an unexpected higher-risk signal, particularly among genetically susceptible participants. These findings support the potential value of genetic risk assessment in cardiovascular risk evaluation for highly active individuals and provide new evidence for precision exercise prescriptions.

articles.title: Qi Yin San Liang San prevents gefitinib-induced nociceptive hypersensitivity by modulating TRPV1 channel activity.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Qi Yin San Liang San (QYSLS) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula used as an adjunctive therapy for malignant tumors, and has been reported to reduce treatment-related toxicities. Gefitinib-associated nociceptive hypersensitivity remains underrecognized, with its underlying causal mechanism poorly defined. It is unclear whether QYSLS can prevent gefitinib-evoked adverse effect and the underlying molecular mechanism remain unknown. AIM OF THE STUDY: To explore the molecular mechanism of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity and evaluate the preventive effects of QYSLS, with specific investigation of TRPV1 channel activity and CGRP release from dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neuron under this pathological condition. METHODS: A mouse model of gefitinib-provoked nociceptive hypersensitivity was established. QYSLS protection was assessed via pain behavioral tests and DRG histopathology. RNA-seq and network pharmacology were used for target screening. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR), cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) and molecular docking confirmed direct gefitinib-TRPV1 binding. Calcium imaging evaluated TRPV1 channel activity in primary DRG neurons and TRPV1-overexpressing cells. Trpv1-/- mice were used to validate its function. RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence staining and ELISA measured DRG TRPV1/CGRP expression and CGRP release. RESULTS: Gefitinib induced time-dependent declines in mechanical withdrawal thresholds (8.7% of the control at day 28) and thermal withdrawal latencies (55.3% of control at day 28), accompanied by DRG injury in mice. DRG RNA-seq revealed elevated Trpv1 transcripts levels and enrichment of ion channel pathways. Gefitinib triggered TRPV1-dependent elevation of intracellular Ca2+ signals in DRG nociceptive neurons. Calcium imaging, SPR, CETSA, molecular docking and site-directed mutagenesis showed that gefitinib directly activates TRPV1. Residue Y454 is critical for this effect, while it is dispensable for capsaicin-mediated TRPV1 activation, and this activation elicits significant Ca2+ influx, neuronal excitation, and increased CGRP in DRG neurons. Genetic deletion of Trpv1 largely restored pain thresholds and rescued gefitinib-caused neuropathic pain. Oral QYSLS alleviated gefitinib-evoked weight loss, DRG histological damage and nociceptive hypersensitivity (recovered to 50.5% of control for mechanical withdrawal thresholds, and 94.7% of control for thermal withdrawal latency at day 28), accompanied by reductions in gefitinib-triggered DRG TRPV1 and CGRP expression of ∼34.6% and ∼56.1%, respectively. Quercetin and ferulic acid, the key bioactive ingredients of QYSLS, can inhibit gefitinib-induced TRPV1 activation. The analgesic-protective effects of QYSLS were substantially blunted in Trpv1-/- mice. CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies a previously unrecognized mechanism: Gefitinib triggers nociceptive hypersensitivity via DRG TRPV1 direct activation. Residue Y454 is critical for gefitinib- but not capsaicin-evoked TRPV1 activation, and CGRP may act as a downstream effector. QYSLS prevents this nociceptive hypersensitivity largely through TRPV1.

articles.title: Mechanism Investigation of Platycodon grandiflorum Active Ingredients in Regulating Epithelial-Mesenchymal Transition and Airway Remodeling in Asthma via Modulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A Axis and IL-17A/MAPK Pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A.DC. is a traditional Chinese medicinal herb recognized for its dual role as both food and medicine, renowned for its effects of diffusing the lung, alleviating sore throat, promoting expectoration, and facilitating pus drainage. In traditional medicinal practice, it is often used in combination with herbs such as Ephedra sinica , Prunus armeniaca and Glycyrrhiza uralensis utilized to mitigate symptoms associated with asthma, bronchitis, and other respiratory diseases. However, the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of its principal bioactive components in treating asthma remain insufficiently characterized. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the pharmacological effects and elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which triterpenoid saponins derived from Platycodon grandiflorum (PL-TS) inhibit airway epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and attenuate airway remodeling in asthma. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Initially, the chemical constituents of the triterpenoid saponin fraction extracted from Platycodon grandiflorum (Jacq.) A. DC. (PL-TS) were identified by Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometry (UPLC-MS). Subsequently, network pharmacology approaches were employed to predict potential therapeutic targets and core signaling pathways of PL-TS in asthma. An OVA-induced asthmatic mouse model was established for in vivo experiments. Airway hyperresponsiveness (AHR) was assessed via whole-body plethysmography (WBP), and histopathological changes in lung tissues were examined via hematoxylin-eosin (HE), Masson's trichrome, and periodic acid-Schiff (PAS) staining. Human bronchial epithelial cells (BEAS-2B) were utilized to establish an IL-17A-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) model in vitro. Finally, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), immunohistochemistry (IHC), quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and Western blotting (WB) were employed to investigate the modulatory effects of PL-TS on proteins associated with airway remodeling, the IL-17A/MAPK signaling pathway, and the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis in both asthmatic mice and cellular models. RESULTS: UPLC-MS/MS analysis identified 38 triterpenoid saponins from PL-TS, providing a chemical foundation for subsequent mechanistic studies. Network pharmacology analysis revealed that the principal targets of PL-TS were predominantly enriched within the IL-17A signaling pathway. In OVA-induced asthmatic mice, PL-TS significantly attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, mucus hypersecretion, and collagen deposition in lung tissues, while markedly reducing serum levels of IL-4, IL-5, IL-13, and OVA-IgE in vivo. Furthermore, PL-TS was found to inhibit the activation of the IL-17A/MAPK and Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A signaling pathways in both mouse lung tissue and stimulated cells, while downregulating EMT-related protein Vimentin, Snail, and N-cadherin, upregulating expression of E-cadherin. suppressing the phosphorylation of p38, ERK, and JNK in the MAPK pathway. In addition, PL-TS downregulated Sirt6 expression and reduced RORγt and IL-17A levels, suggesting a potential involvement of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A regulatory axis, although the precise epigenetic mechanism requires further investigation. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrated that the PL-TS significantly alleviated airway inflammation, mucus hypersecretion, and airway remodeling in asthma model. The effects were associated with suppression of the IL-17A/MAPK pathway and downregulation of the Sirt6/RORγt/IL-17A axis, suggesting a potential dual mechanism that highlight its therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Gegen Qinlian Decoction Alleviates DSS-induced Colitis Through Modulation of Intestinal Stem Cell Homeostasis and M1 Macrophage Polarization.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) imposes a significant burden on human health and socioeconomic systems. Gegen Qinlian Decoction (GQD) is an effective formula clinically used for the treatment of IBD. However, the underlying mechanisms of GQD in treating colitis remain incompletely elucidated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of GQD in DSS-induced colitis mice, and explore the underlying mechanisms, thereby providing novel perspectives and strategies for colitis treatment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A mouse colitis model was induced by administering 2.5% dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) in drinking water. The therapeutic efficacy of GQD was assessed by monitoring body weight, disease activity index (DAI), colon length, histopathological damage, inflammatory cytokines, and intestinal mechanical and mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing was performed to reveal the underlying mechanisms. The effects of GQD on macrophage polarization and intestinal stem cells (ISCs) restoration were subsequently examined. RESULTS: GQD treatment significantly alleviated DSS-induced colitis and tissue damage, accompanied by restoration of tight junction protein expression and improvement of mucus barrier function. RNA sequencing suggested that the effects of GQD in colitis mice were closely associated with ISCs and macrophage functions. Experimental validation demonstrated that GQD treatment was associated with increased expression of ISC-associated markers, including AXIN2, and improved goblet cell-associated mucus barrier parameters. Meanwhile, GQD treatment attenuated M1 macrophage polarization, accompanied by decreased inflammatory cytokine levels and alleviation of intestinal inflammation. These effects were also accompanied by reduced SNX10 expression and alterations in Wnt/β-catenin and NLRP3/caspase-1 signaling pathways. CONCLUSION: GQD ameliorates intestinal mucosal barrier function and promotes mucosal healing in DSS-induced colitis mice. These effects are associated with the upregulation of ISC-related markers expression and the inhibition of M1 macrophage polarization.

articles.title: Simiao Pill ameliorates collagen-induced arthritis in association with gut-joint axis modulation and attenuation of cGAS-STING signaling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Simiao Pill formula (SM), composed of Phellodendron chinense C.K.Schneid., Atractylodes lancea (Thunb.) DC., Achyranthes bidentata Blume, and Coix lacryma-jobi var. ma-yuen (Rom.Caill.) Stapf, is a traditional Chinese herbal formula historically used for damp-heat Bi syndrome and commonly applied to the management of rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-related arthralgia symptoms. However, its anti-arthritic mechanisms remain incompletely defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the anti-arthritic effects of SM in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) and examined whether these effects were associated with gut-joint axis-related alterations and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A CIA mouse model was established and treated with SM for 6 weeks. Arthritis severity, joint pathology, bone erosion, serum cytokines, lipopolysaccharide-binding protein, colonic histology, and tight junction proteins were assessed. Gut microbiota and colonic content metabolites were analyzed using 16S ribosomal RNA sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. cGAS-STING pathway proteins were examined in joint and colonic tissues. A separate antibiotic-induced microbiota perturbation cohort was used to assess the contribution of gut microbiota to high-dose SM (SM-H) efficacy. RESULTS: SM reduced arthritis scores and spleen index in CIA mice. It decreased serum IL-6, TNF-α, and IFN-γ levels, increased IL-10 production, and alleviated synovitis, cartilage damage, and bone erosion. SM also improved colonic histological abnormalities, enhanced colonic ZO-1 and Occludin expression, and reduced serum lipopolysaccharide-binding protein levels, suggesting improvement of intestinal barrier-related indicators. Gut microbiota and metabolomics analyses showed that SM-H reshaped gut microbial composition and colonic content metabolic profiles, particularly involving aromatic amino acid and vitamin-related metabolism. Correlation analysis linked representative microbial taxa and metabolites with arthritis severity, inflammatory responses, intestinal barrier markers, and bone parameters. Moreover, SM suppressed cGAS-STING pathway activation in both joint and colonic tissues. Under antibiotic exposure, the anti-arthritic, barrier-related, and cGAS-STING-inhibitory responses associated with SM-H were attenuated. CONCLUSIONS: SM ameliorated CIA in association with coordinated changes in gut microbial composition, colonic content metabolism, intestinal barrier-related indicators, systemic inflammation, and cGAS-STING signaling. Antibiotic exposure attenuated multiple SM-H-associated responses, supporting a contribution of microbiota-associated processes to the therapeutic response, although microbiota-specific causality was not established.

articles.title: Ethnopharmacological basis of Huangqin Tang in colorectal cancer: Repurposing a classical formula to overcome PD-1 resistance via lactylation blockade.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huangqin Tang (HQT), documented in the Shanghan Lun, is traditionally prescribed for "dysenteric disorders" (Li Ji). Modern clinical studies confirm its efficacy against ulcerative colitis and colorectal cancer-associated inflammation, providing a verified traditional basis for investigating its immunomodulatory effects in colorectal malignancy. However, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the regulatory role of lactate-induced protein lactylation in MIF-driven PD-1 resistance and to determine if HQT can reverse this phenotype through metabolic reprogramming. MATERIALS AND METHODS: CT26-bearing BALB/c mice were administered HQT intragastrically combined with intraperitoneal anti-PD-1 antibodies. Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes were profiled by flow cytometry. Integrative transcriptomics and network pharmacology were utilized to screen candidate targets. LC-MS/MS-based lactylomic profiling identified specific modification sites. Lactate modulation assays, and site-directed mutagenesis (NF-κB1 K249R) coupled with rescue experiments were performed in vitro to validate the molecular cascade mechanistically. RESULTS: HQT synergized with anti-PD-1 to suppress tumor growth and prolong survival. This combination remodeled the immune microenvironment, increasing CD8+ T cells and M1-like macrophages while reducing M2 macrophages and MDSCs. Mechanistically, HQT inhibited tumor glycolysis and lactate production. Lactylomic analysis revealed that lactate induced NF-κB1 lysine 249 (K249) lactylation in CD4+ Tregs, driving MIF transcription. Introducing the K249R mutation abolished lactate-induced MIF expression and reversed immunosuppression. HQT effectively reduced NF-κB1 K249 lactylation, disrupting the MIF-driven feedback loop. CONCLUSION: NF-κB1 K249 lactylation acts as a critical post-translational switch linking tumor glycolysis to Treg-mediated immunosuppression. HQT overcomes PD-1 resistance by suppressing this axis. These findings support combining metabolic intervention with immunotherapy and highlight K249 lactylation as a potential biomarker for treatment response.

articles.title: Cycloastragenol suppresses LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and promotes M2 polarization via TLR4/NF-κB signaling and SIRT1-related regulation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Astragalus has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine for tonifying qi and supporting defensive functions. Cycloastragenol (CAG), a characteristic triterpenoid aglycone derived from Astragalus saponins, has emerging pharmacological relevance in immune and inflammatory regulation, but its role in macrophage inflammatory regulation and phenotypic remodeling remains insufficiently defined. AIM OF THE STUDY: To investigate the effects of CAG on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced macrophage inflammation and phenotypic remodeling, focusing on Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling and the involvement of sirtuin 1 (SIRT1). MATERIALS AND METHODS: RAW 264.7 macrophages were pretreated with CAG before LPS stimulation. Cytokine secretion, phenotype markers, and inflammatory signaling were evaluated by ELISA, immunofluorescence, reverse transcription quantitative PCR, and Western blotting. SIRT1-targeting small interfering RNA was used for functional evaluation. Network pharmacology prioritized candidate targets, while two acute inflammatory tissue transcriptomes and a normal human immune atlas provided expression context. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations explored candidate CAG-protein interactions. RESULTS: Compared with LPS alone, CAG at 20 μmol/L reduced TNF-α from 56.15 ± 2.17 to 25.80 ± 1.87 pg/mL and IL-1β from 93.55 ± 2.66 to 44.49 ± 2.85 pg/mL (mean ± standard deviation; both Tukey-adjusted P < 0.0001). At this concentration, CAG decreased inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and CD86 and increased arginase-1 (ARG1) and CD206. Network pharmacology prioritized TLR4 and SIRT1. Wounded human skin and LPS-exposed mouse lungs showed increased expression of the gene encoding monocyte chemoattractant protein-1-induced protein 1 (MCPIP1). The human atlas detected transcripts for these regulators in macrophages and monocytes. CAG attenuated TLR4/NF-κB signaling and partially restored SIRT1 expression. During CAG treatment, SIRT1 silencing increased TLR4 expression, the phosphorylated/total p65 ratio, iNOS, and CD86 and decreased ARG1, weakening the signaling and phenotypic effects of CAG. Docking and simulations suggested possible CAG-protein interactions. CONCLUSIONS: CAG attenuated LPS-induced macrophage inflammation and favored M2-associated phenotypic remodeling, with SIRT1 contributing to these effects. These findings support CAG as a promising Astragalus-derived immunomodulatory candidate and provide a basis for further exploration of its clinical translational potential.

articles.title: Exposure-informed deconstruction of Chaihu Shugan San links tetramethylpyrazine-paeoniflorin to PRKACA-related neurotrophic signaling and brain-gut pharmacology.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Chaihu Shugan San (CSS) is traditionally used for emotional constraint and digestive discomfort. Identifying botanical and constituent contributions to these coordinated actions could clarify its pharmacological basis. AIM OF THE STUDY: To identify an active reduced CSS preparation and investigate its constituent contributions and PRKACA-related signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Botanical screening and recombination were conducted in chronic unpredictable mild stress rats. The selected combination, FCP (Aurantii Fructus, Chuanxiong Rhizoma and Paeoniae Radix Alba), was chemically characterized. Tetramethylpyrazine (TMP) and paeoniflorin (PF) were measured in plasma after single-dose CSS administration and tested at FCP constituent-equivalent oral doses. Hippocampal assays, Prkaca silencing in HT22 cells and JMV2959 co-treatment examined molecular and pharmacological responses. RESULTS: FCP showed the broadest behavioral and gastrointestinal activity among the reduced preparations tested. TMP/PF reproduced selected FCP-associated responses and increased hippocampal cAMP, PKA activity, BDNF, PSD95 and Synapsin-1. Prkaca silencing attenuated cellular neurotrophic and synaptic-protein responses to TMP/PF. Compared with TMP/PF alone, JMV2959 co-treatment reduced gastric emptying, intestinal transit, sucrose preference and hippocampal cAMP, PKA activity and BDNF, whereas plasma acyl-ghrelin and open-field distance did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: FCP retained coordinated behavioral and gastrointestinal actions of CSS, while TMP/PF reproduced a defined component of this pharmacology. Convergent cellular and hippocampal findings support PRKACA-related signaling as a mechanistically relevant component of the constituent response.

articles.title: A psychedelic-rich alkaloid fraction obtained from Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir attenuates somatic and affective symptoms of naloxone-precipitated morphine withdrawal in C57BL/6 mice.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Mimosa tenuiflora (Willd.) Poir. root bark is traditionally used in northeastern Brazil to prepare "Jurema wine", a beverage employed to relieve emotional distress and restore psychological well-being. However, validating its traditional preparations in central substance withdrawal states remains underexplored. AIM OF THE STUDY: To evaluate the ethnopharmacological potential of M. tenuiflora, we investigated the effects of an alkaloid fraction (AF II) from its root bark on somatic and affective morphine withdrawal symptoms in mice, without compromising analgesia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male C57BL/6 mice were used for the tests. Possible interference with morphine-induced analgesia was assessed using the acetic acid-induced writhing test. The animals were made morphine-dependent using a dose-escalation regimen, and withdrawal syndrome was precipitated with naloxone. AF II (3, 6, or 9 mg/kg, s.c.) was administered before withdrawal induction. RESULTS: AF II did not interfere with morphine analgesia. AF II significantly reduced key somatic signs of morphine withdrawal, decreasing jumping and paw tremor without affecting Walk in reverse. During withdrawal, AF II increased exploratory behavior in the open field and modulated anxiety-related parameters. CONCLUSIONS: The AF II from Mimosa tenuiflora, rich in serotonergic compounds, selectively attenuates somatic and affective components of opioid withdrawal in mice without compromising opioid analgesia, supporting its potential as a preliminary candidate for acute opioid withdrawal modulation. These findings provide scientific support for the traditional knowledge surrounding the central psychoactive and restorative properties of M. tenuiflora preparations.

articles.title: m6A-modified hsa_circ_0010996 regulates ferroptosis in anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury cells by binding to EIF4A3.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the expression and functional significance of N6-methyladenosine (m6A)-modified hsa_circ_0010996 in patients with anti-tuberculosis drug-induced liver injury (ADLI) and cellular models, and to elucidate the molecular mechanism by which it regulates ferroptosis in ADLI cells through interaction with eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3). METHODS: The expression levels of hsa_circ_0010996 in the serum of the study population and in HL-7702 cell models were quantified using quantitative real-time PCR (qRT-PCR). Methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP)-qPCR was employed to assess the m6A modification levels of hsa_circ_0010996. The interaction between hsa_circ_0010996 and EIF4A3 was validated via RNA-binding protein immunoprecipitation (RIP) assays. The extent of ferroptosis was evaluated by measuring malondialdehyde (MDA), ferrous iron (Fe2+), and glutathione (GSH) levels. Furthermore, the expression of ferroptosis-related proteins, including glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) and acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4), was analysed by Western blot. RESULTS: Hsa_circ_0010996 was significantly upregulated in the serum of ADLI patients and in ADLI cell models. Overexpression of hsa_circ_0010996 in HL-7702 cells accelerated ADLI progression and promoted ferroptosis. Mechanistically, fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO)-mediated m6A demethylation inhibited the degradation of hsa_circ_0010996. Hsa_circ_0010996 was found to bind to EIF4A3, with both molecules co-localising within the cytoplasm. Importantly, silencing of EIF4A3 alleviated hsa_circ_0010996-induced ferroptosis in ADLI cells. CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the critical role of hsa_circ_0010996 in the pathogenesis of ADLI through the modulation of ferroptosis. Targeting the FTO/hsa_circ_0010996/EIF4A3 regulatory axis represents a promising therapeutic strategy for the prevention and treatment of ADLI.

articles.title: Sustainability in pharmaceutical sciences: A Radesian top-secret to conducting normal science in drug formulation and drug delivery.
articles.abstract: This article is dedicated to one of the Giants of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Professor Thomas Rades, Head of Research at the Department of Pharmacy and Professor in Pharmaceutical Design and Drug Delivery, University of Copenhagen. This article is positioned in "Perspectives", and it is less about detailed technical and scientific approaches and more about the thinking behind them. The protagonist is Professor Thomas Rades. Therefore, using deconstruction, this contribution draws on lessons from his Masterclass account, using what I call Radesian logic to think about sustainability in pharmaceutical sciences, especially drug formulations and delivery, his favorite. It is a view characterized by evidence-based understanding and nuanced, holistic evaluation of technoscientific problems and solutions, leaving little room for unrealistic claims or speculation. Moreover, it avoids fancy relabeling of what might otherwise be deemed normal science. It teaches what sustainability in pharmaceutical sciences is, what it is not, and what it could be, grounded in quality science focused on ethicality, equity, and people-centeredness. He implies that the major sticking points and main features of what can be considered sustainability, by nature, don't receive the much-deserved celebratory status: They consist of the advanced education (teaching and training or the formation of young scientists to ensure continuity in knowledge production), the search for evidence through methodical applications of foundational scientific principles to unveil the complex structures of molecules (basic research), and perhaps the possible production of innovative products that may solve practical problems or have commercial viability (applied research, if any) in that order. This clear structure is necessary because evidence-seeking that situates the university within its responsible raison d'être is the thinking behind the work, which is no ordinary task but one that requires deep commitment, sacrifice, effort, continuity, investments and adaptation to promote equity and wellbeing within planetary boundaries. Labels fade, institutional expectations change, and public health needs mutate, but normal science must protect its integrity to maintain its legitimacy.

articles.title: Transfer of off-line calibration models to an in-line near-infrared high-speed monitoring system for tablet uniformity.
articles.abstract: In-line near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is a widely used method to monitor tableting processes. The acquisition of in-line NIR spectra of individual tablets is possible between their compression and ejection stages in the tablet press. It was shown, that in-line spectra used for the API content prediction with off-line calibration models led to a systematic prediction bias. To further investigate factors that may influence this bias, in the present study off-line calibration models were developed with tablets of different densities obtained by varying the compression force which were exposed to either room temperature or a range between 22.3 and 51.5°C during spectral acquisition. Univariate (linear response correction) and multivariate (direct orthogonalization) calibration transfer methods were investigated using off-line and in-line acquired calibration and test spectra with different API contents. The different densities of the calibration tablets and the temperature during calibration had a negligible influence on the calibration models and on the cross-validation results. However, both influencing factors had a major effect on the content prediction bias obtained with in-line spectra. Both, calibration transfer methods as well as the off-line calibration with tablet densities and temperatures similar to those during the in-line spectra acquisition reduced the systematic prediction bias successfully.

articles.title: Reversal of gut dysbiosis-related arachidonic acid deficiency alleviates Parkinsonian motor deficits and neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been increasingly implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), but the relationship of microbiota-associated metabolic alterations to PD remains poorly understood. This study investigated the association between gut microbiota dysbiosis and arachidonic acid (AA) dysregulation in PD and evaluated whether modulation of AA homeostasis could ameliorate Parkinsonian phenotypes. Gut microbial alterations were characterized by 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and serum metabolic changes were assessed using untargeted metabolomics combined with microbiota-metabolite correlation analysis. Marked gut microbiota dysbiosis was observed in PD mice and was accompanied by reduced serum AA levels. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) increased serum AA levels and improved motor performance, providing functional support for a link between gut microbiota alterations and disrupted AA homeostasis. In addition, exogenous AA supplementation attenuated motor dysfunction and neuroinflammation. Collectively, these findings support a functional association among gut microbiota dysbiosis, altered AA homeostasis, and Parkinsonian phenotypes, suggesting that modulation of gut microbiota composition or AA availability may represent potential strategies for alleviating PD-associated motor dysfunction and neuroinflammation.

articles.title: Pharmacological characterization of clinical candidate CORT118335 (miricorilant), a selective glucocorticoid receptor modulator, in short-term preclinical models for MASLD.
articles.abstract: CORT118335 (miricorilant) is a selective glucocorticoid receptor (GR) modulator (SGRM) that is currently being evaluated in clinical trials for the treatment of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), based on strong efficacy in mouse models. We reveal gene-specific GR modulation by CORT118335 in the mouse liver. In cell-based models, we evaluated the biological activity of CORT118335 metabolites. Metabolite CORT118335-P9a showed potent GR agonism, while metabolite CORT118335-P9b was largely inactive. CORT118335-P9a concentrations in the mouse liver were very low, and therefore neither metabolite is likely to contribute to the beneficial effects of CORT118335 in vivo. We investigated various aspects of CORT118335 activity in reducing lipid levels in the mouse liver using a model of short-term high-fat diet feeding. Daily administration of CORT118335 appeared to lower hepatic triglyceride rapidly within several days after treatment initiation, specifically in male mice, and these effects were reversed after 7 days of treatment discontinuation. No synergy was observed between the lipid-lowering effects of CORT118335 and the TRβ agonist VK2809 or the PPARγ agonist pioglitazone. At a dose of 6 mg/kg/day, CORT118335 induced evident transcriptional effects with modest lowering of hepatic triglyceride levels, while higher doses induced a more pronounced lipid lowering but less ongoing transcriptional activity for hepatic lipid metabolism genes. Altogether we substantiate the potential of selective GR modulation using CORT118335 as a lipid-lowering strategy in MASLD and highlight the complexity of SGRM-mediated hepatic lipid lowering.

articles.title: Tilianin counteracts doxorubicin-induced myocardial injury by downregulating mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis.
articles.abstract: Doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity (DIC) remains a major clinical limitation of this widely used chemotherapeutic agent. Dracocephalum moldavica L., a traditional Uyghur medicinal herb used for cardiovascular disorders, contains the flavonoid Tilianin (Til). Although Til exhibits reported cardioprotective properties, whether and how it mitigates DIC remains incompletely understood. In this study, we established DIC models in H9c2 cardiomyocytes and C57BL/6N mice and performed transcriptomic profiling to identify underlying mechanisms. Pharmacological interrogation using mitochondrial modulators (carbonyl cyanide m-chlorophenylhydrazone and cyclosporin A) and a ferroptosis inhibitor (ferrostatin-1) revealed that DOX triggers excessive mitophagy, leading to mitochondrial iron release and lipid peroxidation, ultimately driving mitophagy-dependent ferroptosis in cardiomyocytes. Til intervention attenuated DOX-induced cardiac dysfunction and myocardial injury in vivo and protected H9c2 cells from cytotoxicity in vitro by suppressing overactivated mitophagy and partially restoring iron homeostasis. These findings demonstrate that Til confers cardioprotection against DIC through modulation of the mitophagy-ferroptosis axis, supporting its potential as a candidate agent for managing chemotherapy-related cardiac injury.

articles.title: LY294002 and LY303511 exhibit features of the serotonin 5-HT2C receptor ligands.
articles.abstract: Small molecules such as agonists and antagonists, inhibitors, modulators, and blockers are widely used to analyze intracellular signaling pathways and gain insight into molecular mechanisms underlying diverse physiological processes. Unfortunately, the challenge is that many, if not all, of these molecules can affect cellular functions not only by acting on specific cellular targets but also by causing side effects. In particular, the class I phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor LY294002 and its PI3K-inactive structural analog LY303511 have been shown to affect agonist-induced Ca2+ signaling in cells of various types independently of PI3K activity. Here we studied serotonin-induced Ca2+ signaling in HEK293 cells expressing the recombinant mouse 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin) receptor subtype 2C and analyzed the effects of LY294002 and LY303511 on cell responsiveness. As shown with Ca2+ imaging, both LY294002 and LY303511 affected intracellular Ca2+ but via distinct mechanisms. LY294002 suppressed responsiveness of assayed cells to serotonin in a manner suggesting that this substance acted as a competitive antagonist of the 5-HT2C receptor. In turn, LY303511 itself triggered Ca2+ transients in 5-HT2C-positive cells, exhibiting traits of a 5-HT2C agonist. In support of these findings, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations validated that LY303511 binds to the same site on the receptor as serotonin, although LY294002 occupies the vestibule, a region providing ligands access into the orthosteric site, thereby presumably preventing the proper serotonin binding. Altogether, physiological findings and computational data suggested that the observed effects of these compounds were most likely mediated by extracellular mechanisms associated with the interaction of both with the 5-HT2C receptor. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: PI3K inhibitor LY294002 and its phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase-inactive analog LY303511 are shown to exhibit pharmacological properties characteristic of competitive antagonist and agonist of the serotonin 5-HT2C receptor, respectively. These findings could be useful for safety profiling of these compounds and their derivatives, and for studying serotonin-induced signaling.

articles.title: Combination of IL-1β and IL-6 triggers parkinsonian-like tremor in rats: correlation of the effect with noradrenaline levels in the locus coeruleus and ventral anterior thalamic nucleus.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: One of parkinsonian signs is tremor; the mechanism of this dysfunction is unclear. There are indications that IL-1β, IL-6, and noradrenaline (NA) located in the locus coeruleus (LC) and thalamus participate in regulation of parkinsonian tremor (PT). OBJECTIVES: We sought i) to determine the ability of IL-1β and IL-6 to induce tremulous jaw movements (TJMs), a rat model of PT; and ii) to characterize a link between TJMs development and NA metabolism in the LC and some thalamic nuclei. METHODS: Experiments were conducted in male Wistar rats of 530-570 days of age. IL-1β and IL-6 were injected intracerebroventricularly for 10 day at 1.0-25.0 pg and 10.0-250.0 pg, respectively; concentrations of NA and its metabolite 3,4-dihydroxyphenylglycol (DHPG) were determined by HPLC. TJMs were counted by standard method. RESULTS: Interleukins administered separately were ineffective; in contrast, IL-1β at 25.0 pg combined with IL-6 at 250.0 pg significantly stimulated TJM response and increased NA, DHPG, and DHPG/NA ratios in the LC and ventral anterior thalamic nucleus (VATN); NA metabolism in the paraventricular and posterior intralaminar thalamic nuclei did not change. The number of TJMs positively correlated with levels of NA in the LC and VATN. The effect of IL-1β-IL-6 combination was reversed by β-antagonist propranolol but not α1- and α2- antagonists terazosin and yohimbine. CONCLUSIONS: The results advance our understanding of the mechanism underlying parkinsonian-like tremor in rats. The presented data suggests that IL-1β, IL-6, and β-receptors are a potential triple-target in therapy of PT.

articles.title: Revisit of the admitted control RND efflux pumps' inhibitor PAβN: use limitations, and structural revelation in complex with MexB.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To bypass the health problem of antibiotic resistance in Gram-negative bacteria, a tempting approach is to use efflux pump inhibitors (EPI) to block the transporters before they expel antibiotics from the cell. One well-known EPI is the phenylalanine-arginine beta-naphthylamide (PAβN). Although it is described as toxic and therefore unsuitable for clinical use, it is highly effective and is commonly used as EPI reference compound in drug development. Nevertheless, the lack of toxicity on several cellular strains in our hands required us to revisit this known RND inhibitor, to redefine its limits. METHODS: The rational design of new EPIs requires the integration of complementary information on their microbiological activity, toxicity toward eukaryotic cells, and description of molecular interaction with their target at atomic resolution. These parameters should also be considered in comparison with those of an established reference compound such as PAβN. Accordingly, the effect of PAβN on Pseudomonas aeruginosa was evaluated by determining the minimum inhibitory concentrations of three β-lactam antibiotics in the presence or absence of PAβN and by defining concentrations that do not perturb the bacterial envelope. Its toxicity was assessed using four human cell lines and multiple cellular endpoints. Finally, the interaction of PAβN with the RND transporter MexB was characterized by cryo-electron microscopy and crystallography. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Microbiological analyses defined concentration ranges in which PAβN can be used to investigate efflux inhibition without causing detectable perturbation of the bacterial envelope. Across the four human cell models, PAβN displayed limited cytotoxicity, whereas β-naphthylamine was markedly more toxic.
