This points to the β-naphthylamide moiety as a potential contributor to PAβN toxicity, possibly resulting from metabolic proteolysis processing. Structural analyses revealed PAβN bound to MexB in the Tight conformation in both cryo-EM and crystal structures, but at distinct positions within the binding cavity. Comparison with the previously reported structure of PAβN bound to the artificially symmetric trimer of AcrB provides new insights into PAβN recognition and handling by RND pumps. Together, these microbiological, toxicological, and structural data refine the use of PAβN as a reference EPI and provide new perspectives on substrate transport by RND efflux pumps.

articles.title: SCOPE-based target and pathway enrichment identifies the histamine H1 receptor as a regulator of exodosis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Phenotypic screening enables discovery of small molecules without requiring predefined targets, but mechanistic interpretation remains challenging due to polypharmacology and pathway complexity. METHODS: We developed SCOPE (Screening Compound Ontology for Pathway Enrichment), a KNIME-based computational framework that links compound-level screening data to annotated targets and pathways to facilitate generation of mechanistic hypotheses. SCOPE integrates multi-source target annotations and performs sequential target- and pathway-level statistical enrichment using the screened compound library as the background to prioritize shared mechanisms of action. RESULTS: Applied to a previously established high-throughput screen for modulators of endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-stress induced secretion of ER resident proteins, a process known as exodosis, SCOPE identified calcium signaling as the most enriched KEGG pathway without prior biological context. Its target enrichment revealed several G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) linked to inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate receptors (IP3Rs)-mediated calcium signaling, with widespread antagonism of these receptors among compounds that reduced exodosis, implicating this pathway in the regulation of exodosis. Notably, SCOPE uncovered a novel role for the histamine receptor HRH1 in exodosis, which was validated by RNAi knockdown, gene knockout, and pharmacological modulation, implicating HRH1 as a potential therapeutic target for modulating exodosis. DISCUSSION: These results highlight SCOPE's potential to prioritize experimentally testable targets and pathways from phenotypic screening data.

articles.title: The inhibitory effect of gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal on platelet function through regulating outside-in signaling of αIIbβ3 integrin.
articles.abstract: The gadolinium-conjugated diflunisal derivative ETN102 has previously been shown to suppress cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) levels, reduce glial activation, and attenuate neuronal damage associated with stroke. In the present study, we investigated whether ETN102 modulates platelet aggregation and activation. ETN102 selectively inhibited thrombin-induced platelet aggregation while sparing platelet responses to other agonists, including collagen, adenosine diphosphate (ADP), and U46619. ETN102 also reduced adenosine triphosphate (ATP) secretion under aggregating conditions without altering thromboxane B2 (TXB2) generation, suggesting that its antiplatelet effect is independent of the COX-1-dependent thromboxane signaling. Flow cytometric and biochemical analyses further demonstrated that ETN102 suppressed thrombin-induced αIIbβ3 integrin activation, platelet spreading, clot retraction, and the phosphorylation of focal adhesion kinase (FAK) and proline-rich tyrosine kinase 2 (Pyk2), without affecting granule secretion, intracellular Ca2+ mobilization, or phosphorylation of Syk, PI3K, and AKT signaling molecules. In vivo, ETN102 significantly prolonged carotid artery occlusion time in a ferric chloride (FeCl3)-induced thrombosis model and increased tail bleeding time and hemoglobin content. In addition, ETN102 reduced infarct volume and improved neuronal survival markers in a murine model of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury. These findings demonstrate that ETN102 is a thrombin-context selective modulator of platelet integrin αIIbβ3 outside-in signaling, with antithrombotic and neuroprotective potential.

articles.title: Inhibition of cytochrome P450 activities by juglone in human and rat liver microsomes: kinetic characterization and implications for natural product-drug interaction assessment.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Juglone is a redox-active constituent of walnut green husks, but its effects on drug-metabolizing cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We evaluated juglone against six CYP activities in human and rat liver microsomes (HLMs and RLMs) using cocktail probe assays, time-dependent inhibition experiments, kinetic analyses, and molecular docking. RESULTS: In HLMs, CYP2C9 was the most susceptible activity (IC50 = 8.12 μM; K i = 4.97 μM) and showed competitive inhibition. CYP2E1 was the next most susceptible activity (IC50 = 12.67 μM; K i = 19.59 μM; αK i = 8.74 μM) and showed mixed inhibition. In RLMs, CYP1A2 (IC50 = 12.03 μM) and CYP2E1 (IC50 = 18.50 μM) met the prespecified criterion for further kinetic analysis. Subsequent analyses identified mixed inhibition of CYP1A2 (K i = 12.31 μM) and competitive inhibition of CYP2E1 (Ki = 19.89 μM). No consistent progressive loss of activity was observed during preincubation for up to 20 min under the tested conditions. CYP2E1 showed numerically similar apparent K i values but different fitted inhibition models in HLMs and RLMs. However, differing assay conditions precluded attributing these findings solely to species. Molecular docking provided qualitative structural insight into the potential interactions between juglone and CYP2C9. CONCLUSION: Juglone inhibited CYP activities in vitro, with CYP2C9 showing the greatest susceptibility among the six human CYP activities tested. These findings characterize biochemical inhibition and provide a basis for evaluating potential metabolic interactions involving juglone-containing products.

articles.title: Multi-omics and machine learning based on clinical samples: revealing the toxicity characteristics in adverse reactions to Evodia rutaecarpa.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Evodia rutaecarpa (EVR) is a widely used low-toxicity traditional Chinese medicine in clinical practice. Its adverse reactions are often subtle with prominent inter-individual variability, and the associated risks are frequently underestimated. This study conducted multi-omics analysis of the metabolic and microbiological characteristics of its related adverse reactions, and constructed a prediction model to provide a reference for individualized safe medication. METHODS: 86 patients with gastric diseases receiving EVR-containing compound formulas were enrolled and divided into a control group (n = 50) and an adverse reaction group (n = 36) based on the presence or absence of adverse reactions. Serum, urine, and saliva samples were collected for untargeted metabolomics and 16S rRNA sequencing, respectively. Seven machine learning algorithms (logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, etc.) were employed to construct predictive models in combination with LOOCV, screen key features, and derive a multi-omics joint prediction formula. RESULTS: Clinically, adverse events related to EVR predominantly presented as upper-gastrointestinal symptoms. Omics profiling of patient samples identifies tentative correlative trends between EVR-associated adverse events and systemic changes including disturbed amino acid metabolism, shifted neuroactive molecule profiles, altered bile secretion signatures and oral microbiota dysbiosis. Machine learning screening yields multiple model-associated classification features from multi-omics datasets. Serum PE (P-18:1/22:0), hydroxyisocaproic acid and ureidoisobutyric acid show statistical trends linked to lower model prediction outputs for adverse events. Urinary 1, 3-Dihydro-(2H)-indol-2-one and MG (0:0/20:4/0:0) correlate with reduced predictive values, whereas arachidoyl ethanolamide associates with elevated model prediction scores. Higher relative abundances of Granulicatella, Alysiella, Leptotrichia hongkongensis and Streptococcus in saliva correspond to higher predictive probabilities from the classification model. An AUC-weighted multi-omics joint formula is established to calculate individual predictive likelihood of EVR-related adverse reactions. Scores ≥ 0.597 indicate higher model-derived predictive tendency, while scores below 0.597 indicate lower predictive possibility. CONCLUSION: The ten omics-derived discriminative features and the multi-omics joint prediction formula developed in this work enable quantitative estimation of individual-level risk for EVR-related adverse reactions. They offer preliminary references for safety assessment, risk stratification, and personalized application of low-toxicity traditional Chinese medicines.

articles.title: Novel adamantane-nitrone hybrids: design, synthesis, and their multi-target neuroprotective effects against ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Ischemic stroke involves interconnected pathological processes, including calcium overload, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation. This complexity challenges therapies directed at a single target, while limited blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability can restrict drug delivery to the brain. This study aimed to develop hybrid compounds with favorable BBB permeability and multi-target neuroprotective activity. METHODS: Four adamantane-nitrone hybrids (TA1-TA4) were synthesized and screened for cytotoxicity and neuroprotective activity, leading to the selection of TA1. TA1 was then evaluated for its effects on calcium overload, oxidative stress, mitochondrial function, and BBB permeability in vitro, and for therapeutic efficacy and related signaling pathways in MCAO mice. Single-dose safety was assessed separately. RESULTS: TA1 showed the highest neuroprotective activity and lowest cytotoxicity among the four hybrids. It reduced calcium overload, scavenged ROS and ONOO-, and stabilized mitochondrial membrane potential. TA1 exhibited favorable BBB permeability (Papp = 6.73 × 10-6 cm/s) and ameliorated ischemia-induced barrier disruption. In MCAO mice, intravenous TA1 reduced cerebral infarct volume from 32.97% to 14.33%, outperforming the positive control TBN. It also alleviated brain edema and improved neurobehavioral outcomes. TA1 modulated the Bax/Bcl-2/caspase-3, Nrf2/HO-1, and NF-κB pathways. No overt abnormalities were observed in the measured hematological, biochemical, or histopathological indices 48 h after a single intravenous dose of 136 μmol/kg. DISCUSSION: TA1 combines favorable BBB permeability with multi-target anti-apoptotic, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory effects, supporting its further investigation as a candidate for ischemic stroke treatment.

articles.title: Zaizao Shengxue capsule for anemia: a prospective multicenter real-world study of hemoglobin response and predictive modeling.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim in this study was to characterize the 8-week hemoglobin response among patients with anemia receiving Zaizao Shengxue capsule (ZSC) in real-world care and develop and externally evaluate a model for estimating the individual probability of response. METHODS: This prospective multicenter study included 440 patients from 14 centers who received ZSC for 8 weeks. Response was defined as an increase in hemoglobin of at least 20 g/L from baseline at week 8. The development cohort (n = 338) was divided into a training cohort (n = 238) and an internal validation cohort (n = 100). Baseline predictors were selected in the training cohort. Ten candidate models were trained using different algorithms and compared in the internal validation cohort. After model selection and locking, the final model was independently evaluated in 102 patients from four external centers. SHAP and LIME were used for model interpretation. RESULTS: Overall, 204 of 440 patients (46.4%) achieved an 8-week hemoglobin response. Response rates varied across anemia etiologies: 24.0% in cancer-related anemia (60/250), 74.4% in iron-deficiency anemia (67/90), and 77.0% in anemia of chronic disease (77/100). Anemia etiology, age, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were retained as predictors in the final Extra Trees model. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI, 0.729-0.902) in internal validation and 0.769 (95% CI, 0.670-0.860) in external validation. SHAP analysis identified anemia etiology as the largest contributor to model predictions, followed by age and eGFR. CONCLUSION: Eight-week hemoglobin response varied across anemia etiologies among patients receiving ZSC. A model incorporating anemia etiology, age, and eGFR may support individualized pretreatment estimation of response probability based on routinely available clinical information.

articles.title: Glucocorticoid receptor modulation as a host-directed strategy for inflammatory priming across chronic disease states.
articles.abstract: Chronic inflammation is increasingly recognized as a shared feature across neuropsychiatric, neurodegenerative, metabolic, oncologic, and post-infectious disorders, yet treatments mainly target downstream effects. Evidence suggests dysregulated glucocorticoid receptor (GR; encoded by NR3C1) signaling may regulate inflammation upstream, linking stress, HPA axis dysfunction, altered neuroimmune signaling, NF-κB activation, and ongoing inflammation. We review evidence supporting selective modulation of GR as a host-directed therapy targeting this shared mechanism. Across experimental systems, GR modulation is associated with attenuation of NF-κB-associated inflammatory signaling while preserving host-defense and repair-associated pathways. Exploratory clinical observations suggest that biological and therapeutic responses may depend on the degree of GR modulation, providing a hypothesis for prospective evaluation of a potential therapeutic window. Despite remaining questions, convergent evidence views dysregulated GR signaling as a promising upstream target across conditions like post-infectious inflammation, neuropsychiatric disorders, addiction, metabolic disease, and some cancers. We propose a biomarker-guided framework to evaluate selective GR modulation to restore the balance of inflammation in patient groups, rather than just suppressing downstream effects.

articles.title: Cardamonin attenuates SH-SY5Y neuronal apoptosis induced by LPS-activated microglia via modulation of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-κB pathway.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Microglial activation-induced neuroinflammation plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of neurodegenerative diseases. Cardamonin (CD, 2',4'-dihydroxy-6'-methoxychalcone), a natural chalcone flavonoid present in several medicinal plants, demonstrates significant anti-inflammatory activity. Nevertheless, the precise mechanisms by which it mitigates neuroinflammation remain incompletely understood. METHODS: In this study, the potential targets and pathways of CD were investigated using network pharmacology and molecular docking. The neuroinflammatory protective mechanisms were examined in vitro using LPS-stimulated BV2 cells and a BV2/SH-SY5Y co-culture system, employing ELISA, RT-qPCR, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and other assays. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: Network pharmacology identified epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), rac-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase (AKT1), heat shock protein 90 alpha family class B member 1 (HSP90AB1), prostaglandin-endoperoxide synthase 2 (PTGS2/COX-2) and transcription factor p65 (RELA) as key potential targets, with the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1, MAPK/ERK, and NF-κB signaling pathways being the main enriched pathways. In BV2 cells, CD suppressed LPS-induced production of IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and nitric oxide (NO), and modulated the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-κB signaling axis. Pharmacological inhibition of EGFR or PI3K phenocopied the effects of CD, supporting the functional involvement of this pathway. Additionally, CD attenuated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation and prevented the loss of mitochondrial membrane potential. In a co-culture model, CD pretreatment reduced BV2-conditioned medium neurotoxicity toward SH-SY5Y neurons. Collectively, these findings suggest that CD alleviates neuroinflammation through modulation of the EGFR/PI3K/AKT1/ERK/NF-κB pathway, mitigating inflammatory and oxidative stress responses and providing indirect neuroprotection, supporting its potential application in neuroinflammation-associated neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Optical coherence tomography guided targeted non-viral optical delivery of opsin-encoding genes into the retina.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Retinal degenerative diseases cause progressive photoreceptor loss while leaving populations of inner retinal neurons available for optogenetic intervention. However, efficient and spatially controlled non-viral gene delivery to these surviving cells remains challenging. We evaluated optical coherence tomography (OCT)-guided nano-enhanced optical delivery (NOD) for targeted delivery of the multi-characteristic opsin MCO-020 to the degenerative retina. METHODS: NOD uses plasmonic gold nanorods (GNRs) and a 980-nm near-infrared laser to transiently permeabilize cell membranes and facilitate localized plasmid delivery. Delivery parameters were initially optimized in HEK293 cells. In vivo efficacy and safety were subsequently evaluated in rd1 mice following intravitreal administration of MCO-020 plasmid and GNRs followed by OCT-guided laser delivery. Transgene expression, retinal structure, retinal and cortical electrophysiological responses, intraocular pressure, retinal-cell viability, and biodistribution were evaluated. RESULTS: In vitro studies demonstrated laser-dependent and spatially restricted MCO-020 expression without detectable cytotoxicity within the tested operating range. In vivo, OCT-guided NOD produced MCO-020 expression in inner retinal cells within targeted retinal regions without detectable changes in retinal structure or thickness. MCO-020-treated mice demonstrated increased light-evoked retinal and visually evoked cortical responses compared with untreated controls, with responses and transgene expression remaining detectable through the 52-week observation period. Retinal-cell viability, intraocular pressure, and complementary electrophysiological safety assessments showed no detectable treatment-associated adverse effects. Biodistribution analysis showed only low levels of vector DNA in evaluated non-target tissues. DISCUSSION: These findings demonstrate that OCT-guided NOD can provide spatially targeted, non-viral delivery of an opsin-encoding plasmid to the degenerative retina while preserving retinal structure and supporting sustained functional engagement of the visual pathway. The approach may provide a platform for localized delivery of therapeutic genes to retinal regions affected by degeneration.

articles.title: Inhibition of heat shock protein 90 in the mouse spinal cord enhances opioid antinociception via the upregulation of dual specificity protein phosphatase 15 (DUSP15) in CGRP neurons.
articles.abstract: In an extended series of studies, we have shown that Heat shock protein 90 (Hsp90) has a novel role in regulating opioid signal transduction and antinociception in both the brain and spinal cord. Inhibition in the spinal cord enhances opioid antinociception, which led to the finding that an isoform-selective Hsp90 inhibitor could improve opioid therapy, both enhancing pain relief and reducing side effects. However, the signaling mechanisms for this activity are still not fully understood. We thus identified Dual Specificity Phosphatase 15 (DUSP15) from an earlier proteomic study as a protein enhanced in the spinal cord after Hsp90 inhibition. Using male and female CD-1 mice, we confirmed that DUSP15 is upregulated in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord after Hsp90 inhibitor (17-AAG) treatment. Using CRISPR and siRNA-mediated knockdown, we showed that DUSP15 was necessary for the enhanced morphine antinociception after Hsp90 inhibitor treatment in both the tail flick and post-surgical paw incision pain models. Using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and behavioral tools, we placed DUSP15 upstream of both ERK MAPK and AMPK in the opioid signaling cascade. We then used IHC to demonstrate that DUSP15 upregulation occurs at least in part in CGRP neurons, and using cell-selective CRISPR, showed that DUSP15 in CGRP neurons is necessary for the enhanced antinociception observed with spinal Hsp90 inhibitor treatment. Together these studies further expand the known mechanisms by which Hsp90 regulates opioid signal transduction and pain relief and provide basic science insight into a potential strategy to improve opioid therapy using Hsp90 inhibitors.

articles.title: Population pharmacokinetic modeling of voriconazole based on real-world data for dosing regimen optimization.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study established a population pharmacokinetic model of voriconazole with the aim of adjusting the dosing regimen of voriconazole. METHODS: This was a retrospective study in which clinical data from 3,002 patients were collected from their medical records. Based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria, this study included data from 96 patients to establish a population pharmacokinetic model. Following model evaluation, a dosing adjustment regimen for voriconazole was derived using Monte Carlo simulation and validated in a clinical setting. RESULTS: The study used a one-compartment model to fit the data, with a exponential model selected for inter-individual variability and a mixed model selected for residual variability. The model results showed that the CL of voriconazole was 4.2 L/h and the V was 75.9 L. CL was significantly correlated with creatinine clearance (CCr), and C-reactive protein (CRP), while V was significantly correlated with whether omeprazole was used in combination. According to Monte Carlo simulation results: If the trough concentration is <0.5 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be increased by 95%. If the trough concentration is ≥ 0.5 mg/L and <1.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be increased by 65%. If the trough concentration is > 5.5 and ≤7.5 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 35%. If the trough concentration is > 7.5 and ≤10.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 55%. If the trough concentration is > 10.0 mg/L, then the maintenance dose should be decreased by 75%. In the clinical validation study, a total of 67 patients met the new inclusion and exclusion criteria and were included in the validation analysis. Of these 67 patients, after up to three dose adjustments based on the recommendations of the population pharmacokinetic model, 61 patients (91.04%) achieved steady-state plasma concentrations within the target range. CONCLUSION: 67 patients participated in the clinical validation study. The results showed that among the 67 patients who followed the standard treatment regimen described in the package insert, 46.3% achieved the target concentration range. After applying the dose adjustment regimen derived from this study, the proportion of patients achieving the target concentration range increased to 91.04%.

articles.title: Design, synthesis of a novel ginsenoside derivative and its protection against acetaminophen induced liver injury via suppressing HIF1α-mediated glycolytic metabolism.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a leading cause of drug-induced liver injury (DILI). Inspired by the synergistic hepatoprotective effects of (20S, 24R)-ocotillol (OC) and lipoic acid (LA), we designed and synthesized OCLA, a novel ginsenoside derivative that has been granted a patent. METHODS: The structure of OCLA was confirmed using HRMS, 1H NMR, and 13C NMR. In vitro protective effects against APAP-induced HepG2 cell death were evaluated. In vivo, mice were treated with 32 mg/kg OCLA, followed by assessment of serum ALT/AST levels, hepatic total glutathione (GSH), oxidized glutathione (GSSG), the GSH/GSSG ratio and histopathological liver damage. Additionally, UPLC-MS/MS was utilized to determine the pharmacokinetic parameters of OCLA in mice plasma and liver tissues. Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic sequencing, along with molecular docking and CETSA experiments, were performed to identify the key pathway and binding targets. RESULTS: OCLA demonstrated superior protective effects against APAP-induced HepG2 cell death compared to OC in vitro. In vivo, OCLA pretreatment significantly mitigated APAP-induced elevation of serum ALT/AST, restored hepatic GSH/GSSG redox homeostasis, and ameliorated histopathological liver damage. Pharmacokinetic analysis demonstrated prominent hepatic accumulation of OCLA, exhibiting substantially higher AUC and Cmax in liver than in plasma. Integrated omics analysis identified the HIF1α signaling pathway as the key target of OCLA. Molecular docking and CETSA further showed that OCLA directly targeted HIF1α, suppressed its expression, and consequently blocked HIF1α-mediated glycolysis-related genes expression (GLUT1, HK1, HK2, PFKL, PFKFB3, ENO1), inflammatory responses (IL-6, TNF-α) and apoptosis-related proteins expression. CONCLUSION: OCLA pretreatment confers protective effects against APAP-induced liver injury primarily by inhibiting HIF1α-associated dysregulation of glycolysis-related molecular signatures and inflammatory responses, showing promising preventive potential for drug-induced liver injury.

articles.title: Notoginsenoside R1 attenuates ischemic stroke via CKLF1-dependent suppression of neuronal metabolic reprogramming.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke, a leading cause of global mortality and disability, results from cerebral blood flow disruption, driving metabolic and neuronal dysfunction. Current therapies-thrombolysis, thrombectomy, and neuroprotectants-are constrained by narrow time windows and hemorrhagic risks. Notoginsenoside R1 (NGR1), a bioactive saponin from Panax notoginseng, exhibits multimodal neuroprotection, yet its mechanistic interplay with metabolic pathways remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: We investigated NGR1's neuroprotective efficacy in ischemic stroke, focusing on its modulation of the CKLF1/CCR5 axis and metabolic reprogramming. METHODS: This study employs a multi-tiered approach integrating in vitro experiments, in vivo animal research, computationally validated target simulations, and gene knockout techniques to systematically elucidate NGR1's regulatory role in key indicators during ischemic stroke treatment. Molecular docking and kinetic modelling first predicted NGR1-CKLF1 binding, subsequently validated via Cellular Thermal Shift Assay (CETSA) and Drug Affinity Responsive Target Stability (DARTS) experiments. In vitro experiments employed a PC12 cell oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) model to evaluate NGR1's neuroprotective effects. CCK-8 assays, live-dead Cell staining, metabolic assay kits, TUNEL and JC-1 staining, Western blot (WB) analysis, and immunofluorescence (IF) co-localization revealed in vitro metabolic reprogramming mechanisms. In vivo experiments employed a permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (pMCAO) model to mimic human ischemic pathophysiology. Neuronal metabolic reprogramming mechanisms following NGR1 treatment were elucidated via TTC staining, neurobehavioral testing, Nissl staining, Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) assays, immunohistochemical (IHC), WB, IF, and Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP). Pharmacodynamic evaluation in the CKLF1-/- rat middle cerebral artery occlusion model, employing ELISA assays and WB analysis, confirmed NGR1's specificity towards CKLF1. RESULTS: Docking and MD predicted a stable NGR1-CKLF1 interaction; CETSA/DARTS supported a direct physical interaction, but binding-affinity constants were not determined. In vitro, NGR1 mitigated OGD-induced metabolic dysregulation, inhibited apoptosis, and enhanced neuronal survival. In vivo experiments demonstrated that NGR1 reduced infarct volume, improved neurological behavior scores, mitigated Nissl body damage, and alleviated inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NGR1 inhibits downstream AMPK/mTOR/HIF-1α-driven neuronal metabolic reprogramming characterized by glycolytic activation by disrupting CKLF1-CCR5 binding. CKLF1 knockout abolished NGR1's therapeutic effects and its role in neuronal metabolic reprogramming, confirming CKLF1 dependency. CONCLUSION: NGR1 alleviates ischemic neuronal injury, at least in part, by interfering with CKLF1/CCR5-associated signaling, thereby attenuating pathological metabolic reprogramming, neuroinflammation, and apoptosis. Clinical relevance requires further validation.

articles.title: Drug repurposing enhances antibiotic activity in multidrug-resistant staphylococcus aureus through modulation of oxidative stress homeostasis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Antimicrobial resistance represents a major therapeutic challenge, particularly in Staphylococcus aureus, and highlights the urgent need for alternative strategies to enhance the efficacy of existing antibiotics. Modulating bacterial stress-response pathways, especially the RecA-mediated SOS response, may provide a promising adjuvant approach to increase bacterial susceptibility to antibiotic-induced stress. METHODS: This study investigated the potential of repurposed FDA-approved drugs to act as antibiotic adjuvants following in silico identification of compounds predicted to interact with the bacterial recombinase RecA. An integrated workflow was applied, combining in silico screening, formulation selection and optimization, biochemical validation, and in vitro antibacterial assays. The selected formulation was evaluated alone and in combination with streptomycin using IC50 determination, oxidative stress assessment, RecA-associated ATPase activity measurement, growth curve, and colony-forming unit enumeration. RESULTS: Among the tested formulations, the selected combination enhanced streptomycin activity against resistant S. aureus, leading to a 2.2-fold reduction in IC50 while showing no marked antibacterial effect when used alone. These findings support its role as an antibiotic adjuvant rather than as a directly active antibacterial treatment. Mechanistic investigation suggested that the potentiation of streptomycin activity was associated with increased oxidative stress and reduced RecA-associated ATPase activity. The improved antibacterial performance of the combination treatment was further confirmed by growth kinetics analysis and colony-forming unit enumeration. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that targeting RecA can increase bacterial susceptibility to antibiotic-induced stress and enhance streptomycin efficacy against resistant S. aureus. This study supports the development of stress-response-targeted antibiotic adjuvant strategies as a promising approach to improve the therapeutic performance of existing antibiotics.

articles.title: Quercetin attenuates acute inflammation and extracellular matrix remodeling after intracerebral hemorrhage: transcriptomics-informed network pharmacology and experimental validation.
articles.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) induces secondary brain injury characterized by neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, oxidative stress, and extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling. Quercetin (QR), a natural flavonoid with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has shown neuroprotective potential; however, the molecular signatures associated with its effects in acute ICH remain incompletely defined. In this study, QR-related target prediction, ICH-associated gene mining, endoplasmic reticulum stress-related gene annotation, and 2 mouse brain transcriptomic datasets were integrated to prioritize QR-associated targets in ICH. Functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, immune deconvolution, receiver operating characteristic (ROC), and molecular docking analyses were then performed. Key predictions were further evaluated in a collagenase-induced mouse ICH model treated with QR or dexamethasone for 24 h, and their disease relevance was assessed using paired perihematomal and remote brain tissues from ICH patients, with serum cytokine profiling performed in ICH patients and healthy controls. Twenty-nine candidate genes were identified and were mainly enriched in TNF and IL-17 signaling, leukocyte migration, stress-responsive programs, and ECM-associated processes. Seven consensus hub genes were prioritized, including Il1b, Mmp9, Timp1, Myc, Fos, Hmox1, and Socs3. Five hub genes in GSE113151 and six in GSE200575 showed high exploratory discriminative performance. Molecular docking suggested putative binding compatibility between QR and several hub proteins. In vivo, high-dose QR reduced brain water content after ICH. QR treatment suppressed perihematomal Il1b, Mmp9, and Fos expression, increased Timp1 expression, and selectively upregulated Hmox1 at the high dose, while reducing circulating IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and MMP-9 levels. In human ICH samples, perihematomal tissues showed increased IL1B, MMP9, TIMP1, and HMOX1 expression; Western blotting further showed increased IL-1β, MMP-9, and TIMP1 protein levels, and immunohistochemistry showed enhanced MMP-9 immunoreactivity. Circulating inflammatory cytokines were also elevated in patients with ICH. These findings suggest that QR is associated with attenuation of acute inflammatory and matrix-remodeling responses after experimental ICH, providing a pharmacological rationale for further target-focused mechanistic studies and long-term preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of intra-articular triamcinolone acetonide in arthritis treatment: a two-decade FAERS and JADER study with machine learning prediction and SHAP-based interpretation.
articles.abstract: Triamcinolone acetonide (TA) is a widely used glucocorticoid for inflammatory diseases, including arthritis. Although intra-articular TA injection provides effective symptom relief, its safety profile in real-world clinical practice remains incompletely characterized. Adverse event reports associated with intra-articular TA injection for arthritis were retrieved from the FAERS database (2004-Q1 2026) and the JADER database (2004-Q4 2025). Disproportionality analyses were performed using four signal detection algorithms, including ROR, PRR, BCPNN, and MGPS. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate signal heterogeneity and robustness. Time-to-onset patterns were assessed using Weibull analysis. Endocrine-related adverse events were further evaluated using multivariable logistic regression and machine learning classification models with SHAP-based interpretation. A total of 738 FAERS reports involving intra-articular TA were identified, covering 27 system organ classes. Multiple established and potential safety signals were detected, including adrenal insufficiency, hyperglycemia, osteonecrosis, bacterial arthritis, postmenopausal hemorrhage, and Cushing's syndrome. Additional potential safety signals included type 2 diabetes mellitus, flushing, erythema multiforme, pemphigus, and septic shock. The strongest disproportionality signals were observed for injection site calcification, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression, injection site atrophy, and Cushing's syndrome. Most adverse events occurred within 30 days after exposure (84.55%), with a median onset time of 5 days (IQR: 2-14). External signal consistency assessment using 112 JADER reports identified eight signals consistent with FAERS findings. Multivariable logistic regression showed that age, sex, therapy type, and reporter type were associated with endocrine-related adverse event reporting. Machine learning models demonstrated good classification performance, with random forest achieving the highest test set AUC (0.864). SHAP analysis identified demographic and treatment-related variables as important contributors to model classification. This study provides a comprehensive real-world pharmacovigilance assessment of intra-articular TA and identifies both established and potential safety signals. Integration of conventional signal detection, regression analysis, and interpretable machine learning approaches may facilitate systematic characterization of TA-associated adverse event patterns and support future safety monitoring.

articles.title: Therapeutic opportunities of marine-derived bioactive compounds against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses.
articles.abstract: Marine ecosystems are a vast, underexplored reservoir of bioactive compounds with unique structural diversity and potent biological activities. Enveloped viruses, including severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), the causative agent of COVID-19, continue to pose significant global health threats, exacerbated by emerging variants, limited therapeutic options beyond vaccines, and challenges such as drug resistance and immune dysregulation. Compounds derived from marine organisms, including lectins (e.g., griffithsin from red algae Griffithsia sp.), sulfated polysaccharides (e.g., iota-carrageenan from red algae Chondrus crispus), polyphenols (e.g., dieckol from brown algae Ecklonia cava), and depsipeptides (e.g., plitidepsin from tunicates), have shown promising antiviral effects in preclinical studies. These molecules primarily act by inhibiting viral entry (via the spike glycoprotein or glycan binding), replication (targeting proteases such as the main protease [Mpro] and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase [RdRp]), or by modulating host immune responses (e.g., reducing cytokine storms or oxidative stress). In vitro, in vivo, and in silico evidence highlights their potential against SARS-CoV-2 and related enveloped viruses (e.g., HIV, HSV, influenza, HCMV), which share mechanistic similarities, including envelope-mediated fusion and RNA-based replication. This narrative review provides a cohesive overview of selected marine-derived bioactive compounds with reported activity against SARS-CoV-2 and other enveloped viruses. It examines their sources, structural features, mechanisms of action, key activity metrics (e.g., IC₅₀/EC₅₀ values), and translational prospects, and addresses challenges such as scalability, preclinical-to-clinical gaps, and sustainability aligned with the European Blue Economy. By integrating recent findings, this review aims to highlight promising leads and guide future research toward innovative, broad-spectrum antiviral therapies.

articles.title: From sepsis to necrotizing enterocolitis with appendiceal perforation: a case report of successful salvage therapy with aztreonam-avibactam in an extremely preterm infant with NDM-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
articles.abstract: Infections caused by New Delhi metallo-β-lactamase (NDM)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae represent a major therapeutic challenge in neonatology, particularly in extremely preterm infants, for whom effective options are limited and dosing and safety data for last-resort agents such as aztreonam-avibactam remain scarce. We report the case of a male infants born at 24+2 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 530 g who developed Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis with poor clinical response to aztreonam combined with polymyxin B. His clinical course was complicated by pulmonary hemorrhage, disseminated intravascular coagulation, necrotizing enterocolitis, appendiceal perforation, and suspected necrotizing fasciitis. Blood and ascitic fluid metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) identified NDM-producing carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae. Given the lack of effective alternatives and ongoing clinical deterioration, off-label intravenous aztreonam-avibactam was initiated as salvage therapy. Marked clinical improvement was observed within 4 days after aztreonam-avibactam treatment, blood mNGS converted to negative by day 6, and skin and gastrointestinal manifestations resolved after 10 days of treatment, and no adverse events considered attributable to aztreonam-avibactam were identified. This case suggests that aztreonam-avibactam may be a viable salvage option for life-threatening NDM-producing K. pneumoniae infections in extremely preterm infants, though prospective pharmacokinetic and safety data in this population are urgently warranted.

articles.title: Recurrent hypofibrinogenemia after reduced-dose tocilizumab rechallenge in rheumatoid arthritis: a case report.
articles.abstract: Tocilizumab (TCZ), a monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-6 receptor, is widely used for the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other inflammatory diseases. Reductions in fibrinogen levels have been reported during TCZ treatment, and some patients develop hypofibrinogenemia. Clinical experience with TCZ re-exposure after such an event, particularly at a reduced dose, remains limited. We report a 76-year-old woman with RA whose disease remained inadequately controlled despite multiple antirheumatic therapies. On 24 April 2026, intravenous TCZ was reinitiated at 400 mg, with a pretreatment fibrinogen level of 3.29 g/L. Approximately 1 month later, fibrinogen had fallen to 0.85 g/L without clinically apparent bleeding. Further TCZ treatment was withheld, and 20 units of cryoprecipitate were administered. Fibrinogen initially increased to 1.99 g/L and subsequently returned to 2.07 g/L during the period without further TCZ exposure. Her RA subsequently became highly active again and remained inadequately controlled despite ongoing conventional antirheumatic treatment. After discussion of the previous adverse event and the potential risks of re-exposure, TCZ was restarted on 19 July 2026, at a reduced intravenous dose of 240 mg; the most recent fibrinogen level before re-exposure was 2.07 g/L. Her joint symptoms and inflammatory markers improved, but 17 days later fibrinogen again decreased to 1.05 g/L, without clinically evident bleeding. The temporal association with TCZ reinitiation in 2026, subsequent recovery during TCZ withdrawal, and recurrence after reduced-dose rechallenge support a probable association between TCZ and hypofibrinogenemia in this patient. This case shows that hypofibrinogenemia can recur despite substantial TCZ dose reduction in a patient with a previous TCZ-associated episode. If TCZ re-exposure is considered clinically necessary, closer monitoring of fibrinogen may be warranted.

articles.title: Design, Synthesis, and CETP Inhibitory Evaluation of Novel P-methoxybenzene Sulfonamides Supported by Molecular Modeling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Hyperlipidemia is a global health concern characterized by elevated blood lipid concentrations, including cholesterol and triglycerides. Cholesteryl ester transfer protein (CETP) plays a crucial role in transferring cholesteryl esters and phospholipids from antiatherogenic high-density lipoproteins to atherogenic low-density and very-low-density lipoproteins. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to synthesize and evaluate 20 p-methoxy-substituted benzene sulfonamides (6a-6j and 7a-7j) as potential CETP inhibitors. METHODS: The compounds were synthesized and structurally characterized using infrared (IR) spectroscopy, carbon-13 nuclear magnetic resonance (13C-NMR) spectroscopy, proton nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR) spectroscopy, and high-resolution mass spectrometry, followed by evaluation of CETP inhibitory activity. Molecular modeling studies were also performed. RESULTS: The biological assay showed that inhibitors 7f-7j exhibited the highest inhibitory activity, achieving 100% inhibition at 10 µM; inhibitor 7j had an IC50 of 0.55 µM. Compounds 6a-6j and 7a-7e showed CETP inhibition of up to 95%. The presence of an additional ring markedly enhanced activity, likely due to the hydrophobic nature of CETP. The docking results supported this finding, indicating that ligand/4EWS complex formation was driven by hydrophobic interactions and hydrogen-bond formation with the amino acid residues H232 and R201. Higher binding scores were observed for series 7a-7j than for series 6a-6j, highlighting the importance of introducing an additional ring to enhance CETP inhibition. Furthermore, pharmacophore mapping confirmed that these analogues matched the fingerprint of active CETP inhibitors. CONCLUSIONS: A series of novel p-methoxybenzene sulfonamides was synthesized and evaluated as CETP inhibitors.

HSPiP, computational, and thermodynamic models-based solubility validation of tofacitinib in PEG400 - water system, shelf-life estimation, and GastroPlus-enabled predictive in vivo performance.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The subcutaneous (sub-Q) delivery of tofacitinib citrate (TOFA) can be a promising alternative to overcome oral associated side effects and complications . OBJECTIVE: The study aimed to address HSPiP based predicted solubility and solubility behaviour of TOFA in various mass ratios (m = 0.0-1.0) of PEG400 in PEG400-water system T = 298.15-318.15 K. METHODS: Hansen solubility parameters were estimated and the experimental solubility data were validated using various models (Van't Hoff, Apelblat, Roseman-Yalkowsky, and thermodynamic models). Finally, the stability study was conducted to estimate TOFA shelf-life, followed by GastroPlus-based predictive in vivo performance in humans. RESULTS: PEG400 addition resulted in reduced δp and δh values up to m = 0.5, which may be correlated to the effective disruption of extensive H-bond network strength and decreased overall polarity of water by PEG400, as predicted in HSPiP. The temperature-dependent solubility was validated with the models. The binary system (m = 0.5) exhibited stable solubility, suitable for sub-Q delivery. The enthalpy-entropy compensation temperature (Tc) was 59.5 °C, suggesting constant ΔsolG° over m = 0.1-0.9 of PEG400. Thus, TOFA solubility and stability were temperature, mass, and pH dependent. GastroPlus software predicted improved pharmacokinetic parameters and extended in vivo absorption following sub-Q delivery at m = 0.5 in humans. CONCLUSION: Thus, a stable sub-Q product can be a promising alternative to the conventional tablet of TOFA.

articles.title: Interaction of the serotonergic system and GPR39 zinc receptor in antidepressant-like response in mice.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Zinc and 5-HT1A receptors have both been implicated in modulating CREB/BDNF/TrkB pathway when exerting their antidepressant-like effects. That pathway is an important regulator of neuroplasticity, shown to be sensitive to serotonergic and zinc-dependent signalling. This study aimed to determine whether co-administration of GPR39 and 5-HT1A receptor agonists produces antidepressant-like responses in mice and whether these effects are associated with changes in proteins of the CREB/BDNF/TrkB pathway and selected serotonergic markers. METHODS: Male CD1 mice received inactive doses of TC-G 1008 (GPR39 agonist, 5 mg/kg) and 8-OH-DPAT (5-HT1A agonist, 1 mg/kg). Antidepressant-like effects following acute, subacute and chronic treatment were assessed using the forced swim test (FST). Western blot analysis examined the levels of CREB-BDNF-TrkB pathway proteins in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. In GPR39 knock-out (KO) mice, chronic 8-OH-DPAT treatment was further evaluated in FST alongside measurements of CREB-BDNF-TrkB, 5-HT1A, 5-HT7 and SERT protein levels in aforementioned structures. RESULTS: Combined treatment with TC-G 1008 and 8-OH-DPAT reduced immobility in the FST across all treatments durations. Neither treatment nor GPR39 expression affected CREB-BDNF-TrkB protein levels. However, chronic co-treatment increased hippocampal SERT levels in wild-type mice, while producing opposite effects on 5-HT7 protein levels in the prefrontal cortex of GPR39 KO mice. CONCLUSIONS: The rapid antidepressant-like effects of combined TC-G 1008 and 8-OH-DPAT treatment appear independent of the CREB-BDNF-TrkB pathway. Differences in SERT and 5-HT7 protein levels between wild-type and GPR39 KO mice suggest that GPR39 modulates serotonergic system responsiveness to antidepressant treatment.

articles.title: In vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and anti-HCoV-229E activities of Jatropha integerrima leaf and stem bark extract and in vivo evaluation of its intravenous SNEDDS in a mouse model.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has highlighted the need for novel antiviral agents with additional therapeutic activities against inflammatory and opportunistic fungal infections, including mucormycosis. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the in vitro antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antifungal, and antiviral activities of ethanolic leaf and stem bark extract of Jatropha integerrima (JIJ) and its in vivo efficacy against Human Coronavirus 229E (HCoV-229E). METHODS: Antioxidant activity was assessed using DPPH and ABTS assays. Anti-inflammatory activity was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated THP-1 monocytes and RAW 264.7 macrophages by analysing TNF-α and iNOS gene expression. Antifungal activity was investigated against Apophysomyces elegans and Rhizopus oryzae. Cytotoxicity and antiviral activity were assessed in A549 cells. Optimized JIJ-containing self-nanoemulsifying drug delivery system (JIJ-SNEDDS) was evaluated in BALB/c mice intranasally infected with HCoV-229E. RESULTS: JIJ exhibited strong antioxidant activity, downregulated TNF-α and iNOS expression, and demonstrated antifungal activity against both fungal pathogens. The extract inhibited viral replication in A549 cells with minimal cytotoxicity. Optimized JIJ-SNEDDS exhibited a particle size of 115 ± 1.4 nm and zeta potential of - 32.7 ± 2.1 mV. In infected mice, treatment markedly reduced lung viral load and histopathological damage. RT-PCR and protein analyses confirmed decreased viral RNA and protein levels. Flow cytometry revealed an increased Th1/Th2 ratio, decreased Th17/Treg ratio, and increased B- and natural killer (NK)-cell populations. Serum interleukin-6 (IL-6) and TNF-α levels were also reduced. CONCLUSION: JIJ-SNEDDS demonstrated promising preclinical antiviral activity against HCoV-229E, accompanied by immunomodulatory and anti-inflammatory effects. These findings warrant further investigation of its therapeutic potential against coronavirus infection and associated inflammatory complications.

articles.title: Development and optimization of a prolonged-release drug delivery system of progesterone for enhancing conception rate: in vitro and in vivo evaluation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and optimize a progesterone-loaded thermosensitive in situ gel system for the sustained delivery of progesterone, aiming to enhance progesterone exposure, pharmacokinetic characteristics and patient compliance in the management of conception failures associated with progesterone deficiency. METHODS: A Central Composite Design (CCD) was utilized to systematically optimize the concentrations of Poloxamer 407 and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC). The formulation was evaluated based on critical response parameters, including gelation time and viscosity. Comprehensive characterization was performed through pH measurement, rheological assessment, and drug content uniformity analysis. Solid-state properties were investigated using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), and X-ray diffraction (XRD). Furthermore, in vitro release kinetics were monitored for 120 h; in vivo pharmacokinetic studies were assessed by LC‒MS/MS method validation; and pharmacodynamic profiles were evaluated in bubalus bubalis compared with a GnRH-based Ov synch (GPG) protocol. RESULTS: The optimized developed progesterone-loaded thermosensitive in situ gel formulation exhibited reproducible thermogelling behaviour within the physiological temperature with an acceptable gelation time of approximately 56 s. Solid-state characterization suggested reduced crystallinity and possible amorphous dispersion of progesterone within the polymeric matrix with no evidence of chemical incompatibility. The system maintained uniformity of drug content (> 95%) and stability. In vitro studies revealed a diffusion-controlled, sustained-release profile (Higuchi model, R2 = 0.9947) for up to 120 h. In vivo results indicated a significant increase in systemic exposure, characterized by a prolonged half-life (11-12 days) and increased Area under the Curve (AUC) and Mean Residence Time (MRT). Pharmacodynamics outcomes showed improved follicular and luteal development, with a conception rate of 50% compared to 33.33% in the control group. CONCLUSION: The developed thermosensitive in situ gel represents a promising, minimally invasive drug-delivery system that offers comparatively higher pharmacokinetic characteristics and enhanced reproductive performance. This sustained-release approach provides a patient-compliant strategy for increasing conception rate to artificial insemination during induced/ synchronized oestrus in buffaloes.

Network Pharmacology and In Vivo Validation Reveal the Potential Protective Mechanisms of Chonggu Granules in Knee Osteoarthritis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Knee osteoarthritis (KOA) is a common degenerative joint disorder characterized by progressive cartilage loss, chronic low-grade inflammation, and oxidative injury. Ferroptosis-associated iron accumulation and lipid peroxidation have been implicated in osteoarthritic cartilage damage. This study investigated the protective effects and potential multi-target mechanisms of Chonggu Granules (CGG) in KOA. METHODS: Network pharmacology and molecular docking were used to identify candidate CGG compounds, targets, and pathways. KOA was induced in rats by intra-articular papain injection. Rats were randomly allocated to the Control, Model, glucosamine hydrochloride (AT), CGG, Ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1), and CGG plus ML385 groups. Cartilage histopathology, mitochondrial ultrastructure, chondrocyte apoptosis, oxidative stress, serum Fe2+ levels, lipid peroxidation, inflammatory cytokines, and the expression of Nrf2 and related antioxidant and ferroptosis-associated molecules were evaluated. RESULTS: Network pharmacology identified 115 overlapping CGG-KOA targets, including the hub target NFE2L2, enriched in pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis. Molecular docking predicted favorable binding between several major CGG compounds and multiple hub targets. In vivo, CGG attenuated cartilage degeneration, mitochondrial abnormalities, chondrocyte apoptosis, inflammatory cytokine production, oxidative stress, elevated serum Fe2+ levels, and lipid peroxidation. CGG also partially normalized the expression of Nrf2, HO-1, GPX4, and other ferroptosis-associated molecules. These effects were partially attenuated by ML385. DISCUSSION: The findings suggest that CGG exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against KOA-related cartilage injury by modulating inflammation, oxidative stress, and ferroptosis-associated processes. The partial attenuation of these effects by ML385 supports the involvement of Nrf2-associated antioxidant signaling and downstream ferroptosis-related responses. CONCLUSION: CGG alleviated KOA-related cartilage injury and ferroptosis-associated oxidative damage through potential multi-target regulation, with Nrf2-associated antioxidant responses contributing to these protective effects.

articles.title: Network Pharmacology and Molecular Docking on the Mechanism of Epimedium in the Treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: To investigate the mechanism of Epimedium in the treatment of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) using network pharmacology and molecular docking approaches. METHODS: The active components and corresponding targets of Epimedium were screened from the Traditional Chinese Medicine Systems Pharmacology (TCMSP) database. COPD-related disease targets were obtained from the OMIM and GeneCards databases. All target genes were standardized using the UniProt database. Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) networks, Gene Ontology (GO) enrichment, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway enrichment analyses were performed using the ClusterProfiler R package and the STRING database. The herb-compound-target network and the target-pathway network were constructed in Cytoscape to identify core compounds, key targets, and major pathways. Finally, molecular docking between the core targets and the active compounds was performed using AutoDock Vina. RESULTS: A total of 23 active components and 223 corresponding targets of Epimedium were identified in the treatment of COPD. The core targets included TP53, IL1B, AKT1, TNF, and IL6. GO enrichment analysis indicated that biological processes were primarily enriched in responses to lipopolysaccharide, molecules of bacterial origin, epithelial cell proliferation and injury repair, and regulation of apoptotic signaling pathways. KEGG pathway enrichment yielded 200 signaling pathways; after excluding irrelevant pathways, the most significantly enriched pathways were predominantly associated with inflammation and immune regulation, including the PI3KAkt, TNF, IL-17, AGE-RAGE, and p53 signaling pathways. Molecular docking results demonstrated that the active compounds of Epimedium exhibited favorable binding affinities with IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF. DISCUSSION: These findings suggest that Epimedium exerts therapeutic effects against COPD through a multicomponent, multi-target, and multi-pathway regulatory mechanism. The integrated network pharmacology and molecular docking analyses indicate that modulation of inflammatory and oxidative stress-related pathways may represent the principal molecular basis underlying its pharmacological activity, providing mechanistic support for future experimental validation. CONCLUSION: Epimedium exhibits the multi-component, multi-target, and multi-pathway characteristics of traditional Chinese medicine. Its therapeutic effects in COPD are mediated through active ingredients such as quercetin, kaempferol, and luteolin, which regulate core targets including IL-1β, IL-6, TNF, and TP53, and modulate inflammation- and immune-related pathways such as PI3K-Akt, AGE-RAGE, and IL-17. These actions collectively contribute to anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative stress effects, regulation of pulmonary apoptosis, and inhibition of pulmonary vascular and airway remodeling. This study tried to apply network pharmacology and molecular docking to elucidate the multi-target synergistic mechanism of Epimedium in the treatment of COPD, providing a theoretical basis for subsequent experimental validation and drug development.

articles.title: Hesperidin Enhances Doxorubicin Cytotoxicity in MCF-7 Breast Cancer Cells: Evidence from Cellular, Gene Expression, Global DNA Methylation, and Molecular Docking Analyses.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVE: Doxorubicin efficacy in breast cancer is constrained by chemoresistance and toxicity. Hesperidin, a citrus flavonoid, exhibits anticancer and epigenetic regulatory properties. This study evaluated whether hesperidin enhances doxorubicin cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells and characterized the associated apoptotic and Heat-Shock (HSP60, HSP90) transcripts, as well as global DNA methylation. METHODS: Cytotoxicity and synergy were assessed using the MTT assay and the Chou-Talalay method (CI). Apoptosis and cell cycle were analyzed by flow cytometry. Expression of BAX, BCL2, HSP60, and HSP90 was quantified using RT-qPCR. Global DNA methylation (5-mC%) was assessed colorimetrically, alongside molecular docking simulations for HSP60 and HSP90. RESULTS: Combining hesperidin with doxorubicin produced synergistic cytotoxicity (CI < 1) and a dosereduction index of 1.95 for doxorubicin. The combination induced apoptosis, accompanied by upregulation of BAX, downregulation of BCL2, and modulation of HSP60/HSP90 transcript levels. Additionally, the combination attenuated doxorubicin-induced global hypermethylation. Molecular docking demonstrated favorable binding affinities of hesperidin toward both HSP60 and HSP90, particularly HSP60; however, these findings remain correlative without proving direct target engagement. DISCUSSION: The synergistic response, paired with modulated apoptotic markers and global DNA methylation, suggests that hesperidin sensitizes MCF-7 cells to doxorubicin through multi-targeted cellular and epigenetic pathways. While docking and transcriptomic shifts indicate potential chaperone involvement, these preliminary observations require further functional validation. CONCLUSION: Hesperidin enhances doxorubicin cytotoxicity in MCF-7 cells by modulating apoptosis, stressresponse transcripts, and DNA methylation. These in-vitro findings support further mechanistic and in-vivo evaluation of this combination strategy.

articles.title: Rivastigmine and Emerging Nanotechnological Strategies for Targeted Delivery: A Comprehensive Review.
articles.abstract: Alzheimer's disease affects millions of people globally; it is an irreversible and incurable disease, characterized by gradual cognitive decline as well as pathophysiological changes including the presence of senile plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. There are several risk factors associated with Alzheimer's disease, including elevated blood pressure, blood sugar concentration, alcohol consumption, smoking, and sleep disturbances. Rivastigmine is an FDA-approved cholinesterase inhibitor used to treat Alzheimer's disease. It is available as oral solutions, capsules, and transdermal patches. Oral administration can lead to detrimental and off-target effects such as nausea and vomiting, and the use of patches can cause irritation and rashes. Across various systems, including the Cardiovascular (CVS), Gastrointestinal (GI), immunological, dermatological, and respiratory systems, rivastigmine has been associated with effects that further necessitate targeted drug delivery. Novel drug delivery systems such as Liposomes, Polymeric Nanoparticles, Dendrimers, Solid Lipid Nanoparticles (SLNs), Nanostructured Lipid Carriers (NLCs), nano-emulsions, and Mesoporous Silica Nanoparticles (MSNs) have been developed to address the limitations of conventional dosage forms. These new formulations possess the ability to increase drug loading capacity, enhance penetration across the BBB, reduce expulsion, and offer controlled release of the drug. As a result, rivastigmine can be targeted to the intended site, with fewer off-target effects. However, formulation-specific toxicity may still occur. Positive off-target effects, such as improved appetite, protection against malnutrition, and evidence of advantage in treating colitis, were also observed with rivastigmine. However, detailed studies of its mechanism of action are needed to provide a scientifically sound justification for repurposing rivastigmine. Google Scholar and PubMed were searched for literature for this review and included studies that met the criteria.

articles.title: In silico Design and Molecular Modeling of Piperazine-Oxadiazole Appended Imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]Thiadiazoles as Promising RTK Inhibitors.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cancer remains a significant global health issue, and the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) is a key therapeutic target in various cancer types. This study aimed to identify new, potent EGFR inhibitors. METHODS: In silico analysis was used to design and evaluate novel Imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives with dual pharmacophores. Molecular docking was performed using Autodock Vina 1.1.2 to assess their binding affinities to EGFR Kinase, VEGFR2, and Human HER2. Pharmacological profiling was also conducted to predict ADMET (Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, Excretion, and Toxicity) and drug-likeness properties. To confirm the stability of the most promising candidates, Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations were performed using Maestro. RESULTS: The docking analysis revealed that all ligands exhibited favorable binding affinities toward the selected receptor tyrosine kinases (1YWN, 3POZ, and 3PP0), with binding energies ranging from -8.3 to -10.4 kcal/mol. Among the targets, 3POZ showed the strongest overall ligand interactions. Notably, Ligand 6c showed superior binding affinity with a maximum docking score of -10.4 kcal/mol (Pose 1). ADMET profiles of all the compounds showed that compounds showed drug likeness in the order of 6a > 6b > 6c as per the Lipinski Rule of Five. DISCUSSION: The designed imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives exhibited stable binding within the EGFR kinase domain, with supportive comparative analysis against VEGFR2 and HER2. Molecular docking and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations confirmed favorable interaction stability. ADMET profiling suggested acceptable drug-likeness and oral absorption. These findings highlight the potential of the proposed scaffolds as promising RTK inhibitors warranting further experimental validation. CONCLUSION: This study employed molecular docking, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, and ADMET profiling to evaluate substituted imidazo[2,1-b][1,3,4]thiadiazole derivatives (6a-6c) targeting VEGFR2, EGFR, and HER2. Among the series, the nitro-substituted compound 6c exhibited the strongest binding affinity and most stable interactions within the kinase active sites. Molecular dynamics results confirmed stable complex formation, as evidenced by consistent RMSD and persistent hydrogen bonding. ADMET analysis indicated favorable drug-likeness and predicted oral bioavailability. Overall, compound 6c emerges as the most promising candidate for further experimental validation as a receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor.
